NetArchTest and ArchUnitNET are the two established open-source libraries for architecture tests in .NET. aweXpect.Reflection covers the same ground (dependency rules, naming conventions, cycle detection) as part of a general reflection assertion library. This page maps the three approaches against each other.
documents.s: Feature comparison with NetArchTest and ArchUnitNET

documents.t: "The presentation layer must not reference the data layer": aweXpect.Reflection NetArchTest ArchUnitNET await That(Types.InNamespace("MusicStore.Presentation")) .DoNotDependOn("MusicStore.Data") .Because("the presentation layer is decoupled from persistence"); No separate loader or result handling: the selection scans the loaded assemblies, and a violation fails the test with a message listing the offending types. var result = Types.InAssembly(typeof(AlbumController).Assembly) .That().ResideInNamespace("MusicStore.Presentation") .ShouldNot().HaveDependencyOn("MusicStore.Data") .GetResult(); Assert.True(result.IsSuccessful); // violations are in result.FailingTypeNames GetResult() returns a TestResult with IsSuccessful and the failing types; turning that into a useful test failure (assertion + message) is left to you. private static readonly Architecture Architecture = new ArchLoader().LoadAssemblies(typeof(AlbumController).Assembly).Build(); IArchRule rule = Types().That().ResideInNamespace("MusicStore.Presentation") .Should().NotDependOnAny(Types().That().ResideInNamespace("MusicStore.Data")) .Because("the presentation layer is decoupled from persistence"); rule.Check(Architecture); // throws with the violations listed The architecture is loaded explicitly (and cached statically); Check comes from a test-framework integration package and throws a FailedArchRuleException describing each violation.
documents.s: The same rule in all three libraries

documents.t: NetArchTest (NetArchTest.Rules) is a deliberately small, type-level rule engine: Types.InAssembly(…) → .That() predicates → .Should()/.ShouldNot() conditions → .GetResult(). It reads assemblies with Mono.Cecil and evaluates everything against TypeDefinitions. There are no member-level rules and no assertion integration: you check IsSuccessful yourself. ArchUnitNET (TngTech.ArchUnitNET) is the .NET port of Java's ArchUnit. It loads assemblies into its own Architecture model (also via Mono.Cecil), on which rules from ArchRuleDefinition (Types(), Classes(), MethodMembers(), …) are checked through per-framework integration packages (xUnit, NUnit, MSTest, TUnit). It is the most feature-rich of the three for pure architecture testing: slices, cycle rules and PlantUML import/export. aweXpect.Reflection works directly on System.Reflection objects inside the aweXpect expectation model: a "layer" is a reusable Filtered.Types selection, an architecture rule is an ordinary await That(…) expectation, and the same vocabulary extends to methods, properties, fields, events, constructors and assemblies for convention tests.

Legend: ✅ built-in · ⚠️ partial or via a general mechanism · ❌ not available. Capability NetArchTest ArchUnitNET aweXpect.Reflection Rule subjects types only types + members assemblies, types + all member kinds Selection by assembly / namespace ✅ ✅ ✅ Naming rules (prefix/suffix/regex) ✅ ✅ ✅ (plus wildcard, custom comparer) Type kinds ⚠️ classes, interfaces ✅ classes, interfaces, enums, structs, records ✅ plus delegates, exceptions, attributes, ref structs, record structs Access modifiers ⚠️ public, nested ✅ ✅ Attribute rules ✅ presence ✅ incl. argument values ✅ incl. typed predicate on the attribute instance Member-level rules (methods, properties, fields) ❌ ✅ ✅ plus events, constructors, parameter modifiers, async, extension methods, operators, required / nullable members Immutability / nullability rules ✅ ⚠️ immutability ✅ type- and member-level Dependency rules (on / not on / only on) ✅ ✅ ✅ Body-level (IL) dependency detection ✅ ✅ ⚠️ signature-level default, IL via custom resolver Dependency cycle detection ❌ ✅ via slices ✅ via namespaces / slice roots Failure messages explain the violation ❌ failing types only ✅ ✅ all violations, grouped per rule Combine rules in one verification ✅ policies ✅ And/Or ✅ Expect.ThatAll Exemptions to a rule ⚠️ custom rule ⚠️ predicates ✅ Except(…) / Except<T>() Test-framework integration ❌ assert manually ✅ xUnit / NUnit / MSTest / TUnit packages ✅ framework-agnostic (aweXpect core) PlantUML diagrams (import/export) ❌ ✅ ❌

The most important technical difference is where dependencies are read from: Signature-level vs. IL-level NetArchTest and ArchUnitNET parse assemblies with Mono.Cecil and walk method bodies: an instantiation (new AlbumRepository()), a static call or a cast inside a method counts as a dependency. aweXpect.Reflection's default resolver works on reflection metadata and sees only the declared signatures (base type, interfaces, member/parameter/return types, attributes; see type dependencies). Body-only references are invisible to it unless you plug in an IL-level custom dependency resolver, e.g. backed by Mono.Cecil. In return, the signature-level default needs no assembly file on disk, never diverges from the runtime types, and filters out compiler plumbing (state machines, synthesized records members, nullability attributes, …) so rules only see code you actually wrote.

aweXpect.Reflection NetArchTest ArchUnitNET // Namespaces under MusicStore must be free of (transitive) cycles, // grouped into one slice per direct sub-namespace of MusicStore await That(Types.InNamespace("MusicStore")) .HaveNoDependencyCycles("MusicStore"); Cycles are reported as namespace chains (e.g. MusicStore.Billing -> MusicStore.Catalog -> MusicStore.Billing); see dependency cycles for the namespace-family and slice-root semantics. // Not supported: NetArchTest has no cycle detection or slice concept. SliceRuleDefinition.Slices() .Matching("MusicStore.(*)") .Should().BeFreeOfCycles() .Check(Architecture); Slices are matched with (*)/(**) namespace patterns; cycle output lists the slice chain and the type-to-type references behind each edge.

What failure of the rule from the top of this page looks like in each library, when AlbumController in the presentation layer references AlbumRepository in the data layer: aweXpect.Reflection NetArchTest ArchUnitNET Failure message Expected that types within namespace "MusicStore.Presentation" in all loaded assemblies all do not depend on namespace "MusicStore.Data", because the presentation layer is decoupled from persistence, but it contained types with the dependency Not matching items: [ AlbumController ] The selection and the rule describe themselves in the message, including the Because(…) reason, followed by the violating types. Assert.True() Failure Expected: True Actual: False Neither the rule nor the violators are part of the message: Assert.True(result.IsSuccessful) reports only the boolean (and a custom user message replaces even that). A useful failure message has to be built by hand from result.FailingTypeNames. "Types that reside in namespace with full name "MusicStore.Presentation" should not depend on any Types that reside in namespace with full name "MusicStore.Data" because the presentation layer is decoupled from persistence" failed: MusicStore.Presentation.AlbumController does depend on "MusicStore.Data.AlbumRepository" The FailedArchRuleException message quotes the rule, including the Because(…) reason, and lists each violating object with a failure description. Several aweXpect rules combine into one verification with Expect.ThatAll(…), which numbers each rule and reports all failures together; see layers as type selections for a full example with output.

NetArchTest stops at types, and ArchUnitNET's member rules cover names, visibility and a few modifiers. Convention tests over member details are where aweXpect.Reflection's filter and expectation vocabulary goes further; the same fluent style covers e.g.: // All async methods end in "Async" await That(In.AssemblyContaining<PlaylistService>() .Methods().WhichAreAsync()) .HaveName("Async").AsSuffix(); // Every public method with an [HttpGet] or [HttpPost] attribute accepts a CancellationToken await That(In.AssemblyContaining<AlbumController>() .Public.Methods().With<HttpGetAttribute>().OrWith<HttpPostAttribute>()) .HaveParameter<CancellationToken>(); // Serializable types have exactly one parameterless constructor await That(In.AllLoadedAssemblies() .Types().With<SerializableAttribute>()) .ContainConstructors(c => c.WithNoParameters()).Exactly(1);
aweXpect.Reflection and FluentAssertions both verify reflection types, with different APIs and feature sets. This page maps what each offers for assemblies, types, and members.

FluentAssertions extends each reflection object with a synchronous subject.Should() entry point and reaches collections through selectors such as assembly.Types() or type.Methods(). aweXpect.Reflection wraps the same objects in an asynchronous await That(subject) call and builds collections from In.* sources (In.AllLoadedAssemblies(), In.AssemblyContaining<T>(), …) that are narrowed with WhichAre*/With* filter chains. aweXpect.Reflection also offers symmetric singular (Is*/Has*) and plural (Are*/Have*) expectations for every target, while FluentAssertions pairs single-subject assertions with a smaller set of selector assertions.

Legend: ✅ dedicated assertion · ⚠️ only via a general mechanism (selector, string assertion, or LINQ) · ❌ no dedicated assertion. Capability FluentAssertions aweXpect.Reflection Assembly: references / dependencies ✅ ✅ Assembly: name ⚠️ ✅ Assembly: version ❌ ✅ Assembly: strong name / signing ✅ ✅ Assembly: target framework ❌ ✅ Type: kind (class/interface/enum/struct/record/…) ⚠️ ✅ Type: abstract / sealed / static ✅ ✅ Type: access modifier ✅ ✅ Type: assignable / implement / derive ✅ ✅ Type: namespace ⚠️ ✅ Type: name ⚠️ ✅ Type: attributes (incl. predicate) ✅ ✅ Type: member presence by signature ✅ ⚠️ Type: operator presence (by kind) ⚠️ ✅ Type: conversion operators by signature ✅ ✅ Type: immutability / member nullability ❌ ✅ Type: dependencies (on / only on / outside an allowed set) ❌ ✅ Method: virtual / async / return type ✅ ✅ Method: static / abstract / sealed / generic / extension / operator ❌ ✅ Method: override ❌ ✅ Method: parameter modifiers / types / counts ❌ ✅ Method: access modifier ✅ ✅ Method: name ⚠️ ✅ Property: readable / writable ✅ ✅ Property: virtual ✅ ✅ Property: static / abstract / required / indexer / init-setter / override ❌ ✅ Property: nullable ❌ ✅ Property: return / declared type ✅ ✅ Constructor: dedicated assertions / filtering ⚠️ ✅ Field: assertions (static / read-only / constant / required / nullable) ❌ ✅ Event: assertions ❌ ✅ The sections below detail each target with side-by-side examples.

FluentAssertions (AssemblyAssertions): Reference/NotReference, BeSignedWithPublicKey/BeUnsigned, DefineType. No assertion for assembly name, version, or target framework; use the string API on assembly.GetName(). aweXpect.Reflection: HasName, HasVersion, DependsOn/DoesNotDependOn/DependsOnlyOn, IsStrongNamed, Targets, Has<TAttribute>; plural equivalents (HaveName, …) over collections. FluentAssertions aweXpect.Reflection assembly.Should().Reference(typeof(string).Assembly); assembly.Should().NotReference(unwantedAssembly); assembly.Should().BeSignedWithPublicKey("0024000004800000..."); assembly.GetName().Name.Should().Be("MusicStore"); // name via string API await That(assembly).HasName("MusicStore"); await That(assembly).DependsOn("System.Core"); await That(assembly).DoesNotDependOn("UnwantedDependency"); await That(assembly).IsStrongNamed(); await That(In.AllLoadedAssemblies()).HaveName("System").AsPrefix();

FluentAssertions (TypeAssertions): Be<T>/NotBe<T>, BeAssignableTo<T>, Implement<T>/NotImplement<T>, BeDerivedFrom<T>, BeAbstract/BeSealed/BeStatic, HaveAccessModifier(CSharpAccessModifier), BeDecoratedWith<T> (with attribute predicate and OrInherit variants), member presence (HaveProperty/HaveMethod/HaveConstructor/HaveIndexer/HaveExplicit*), and conversion operators. Type kind is available only as a selector filter (ThatAreClasses()), and namespace only on the selector (BeInNamespace); a single type's name/namespace use the string API. aweXpect.Reflection: type-kind assertions (IsAClass, IsAnInterface, IsAnEnum, IsAStruct, IsARecord, IsARecordStruct, IsARefStruct, IsADelegate, IsAnAttribute, IsAnException), IsAbstract/IsSealed/IsStatic/IsReadOnly/IsNested/IsGeneric/IsInstantiable/IsImmutable, access modifiers (IsPublic, …), InheritsFrom<T>().Directly(), HasName, HasNamespace/IsWithinNamespace, Has<TAttribute>, quantified member containment (ContainsMethods(), …), member nullability (OnlyHasNullableMembers/OnlyHasNonNullableMembers), type-level dependencies (DependsOn/DoesNotDependOn/DependsOnlyOn/HasDependenciesOutside, against namespaces or type selections), operator presence by kind (HasOperator(Operator), HasOperator<TOperand>(Operator)) and conversion operators by signature (HasImplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>, HasExplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>). FluentAssertions aweXpect.Reflection typeof(Playlist).Should().BeAssignableTo<IPlaylist>(); typeof(Playlist).Should().BeDerivedFrom<PlaylistBase>(); typeof(PlaylistBase).Should().BeAbstract(); typeof(Playlist).Should().HaveAccessModifier(CSharpAccessModifier.Public); typeof(Playlist).Should().BeDecoratedWith<GenreAttribute>(a => a.Name == "Rock"); typeof(Playlist).Namespace.Should().Be("MusicStore"); // namespace via string API // type kind only as a selector filter: AllTypes.From(assembly).ThatAreClasses().Should().BeInNamespace("MusicStore"); await That(typeof(Playlist)).IsAClass(); await That(typeof(IPlaylist)).IsAnInterface(); await That(typeof(Genre)).IsAnEnum(); await That(typeof(PlaylistBase)).IsAbstract(); await That(typeof(Playlist)).HasNamespace("MusicStore"); await That(typeof(Playlist)).Has<GenreAttribute>(a => a.Name == "Rock"); await That(typeof(TrackDuration)).HasOperator(Operator.Addition); await That(typeof(TrackDuration)).HasImplicitConversionOperator<TrackDuration, TimeSpan>(); await That(In.AllLoadedAssemblies() .Types().WhichAreClasses().WhichArePublic()) .HaveNamespace("MusicStore").AsPrefix();

FluentAssertions (MethodInfoAssertions): BeVirtual/NotBeVirtual, BeAsync/NotBeAsync, ReturnVoid/NotReturnVoid, Return<T>/NotReturn<T>, HaveAccessModifier(CSharpAccessModifier), BeDecoratedWith<T>. No assertions for static/abstract/sealed/generic/extension/operator/override, no parameter assertions, and no name assertion (use the string API on method.Name). aweXpect.Reflection: the above plus IsStatic/IsAbstract/IsSealed/IsGeneric/IsAnExtensionMethod/IsAnOperator (incl. a specific Operator, e.g. IsAnOperator(Operator.Equality)), Overrides<T>, ReturnsExactly<T>/DoesNotReturnExactly<T>, HasName, and a parameter family: HasParameter<T>/DoesNotHaveParameter<T>/HasParameterCount/HasInParameter/HasOutParameter/HasRefParameter/HasOptionalParameter/HasParamsParameter (with AtIndex/AtIndexFromEnd/default-value refinements). FluentAssertions aweXpect.Reflection MethodInfo method = typeof(Playlist).GetMethod("PlayAsync"); method.Should().BeVirtual(); method.Should().Return<Task>(); method.Should().HaveAccessModifier(CSharpAccessModifier.Public); method.Should().BeDecoratedWith<ObsoleteAttribute>(); method.Name.Should().StartWith("Play"); // name via string API MethodInfo method = typeof(Playlist).GetMethod("PlayAsync"); await That(method).IsPublic(); await That(method).IsAsync(); await That(method).Returns<Task>(); await That(method).HasName("Play").AsPrefix(); await That(method).Has<ObsoleteAttribute>(); await That(In.AssemblyContaining<Playlist>() .Methods().WhichArePublic().With<TestAttribute>()) .HaveName("Test").AsPrefix();

FluentAssertions (PropertyInfoAssertions): BeVirtual/NotBeVirtual, BeReadable/BeWritable (each with an optional CSharpAccessModifier), NotBeReadable/NotBeWritable, Return<T>/NotReturn<T>, BeDecoratedWith<T>. No assertions for static/abstract/sealed/required/indexer/init-setter/override, and no name assertion. aweXpect.Reflection: IsReadable/IsWritable/IsReadOnly/IsWriteOnly/IsReadWrite, HasAGetter/HasASetter/HasAnInitSetter, IsStatic/IsAbstract/IsSealed/IsVirtual, IsRequired, IsNullable, IsAnIndexer, IsAnExtensionProperty, Overrides<T>, IsOfType<T>/IsOfExactType<T> (and IsNotOfType<T>/IsNotOfExactType<T>), HasName, Has<TAttribute>. FluentAssertions aweXpect.Reflection PropertyInfo property = typeof(Playlist).GetProperty("Rating"); property.Should().BeReadable(CSharpAccessModifier.Public); property.Should().BeWritable(); property.Should().Return<int>(); PropertyInfo property = typeof(Playlist).GetProperty("Rating"); await That(property).HasAGetter(); await That(property).IsWritable(); await That(property).IsOfType<int>(); await That(property).HasName("Rating"); await That(In.AssemblyContaining<Playlist>() .Properties().WhichArePublic()) .HaveName("Id").AsSuffix();

FluentAssertions: no dedicated constructor selector. A constructor is reached through Type.HaveConstructor(parameterTypes) / HaveDefaultConstructor(), after which .Which exposes the ConstructorInfo for HaveAccessModifier / BeDecoratedWith. aweXpect.Reflection: dedicated expectations on a single ConstructorInfo and on collections of constructors, and an In.*…Constructors() filter: IsStatic, the full parameter family (HasParameter<T>/DoesNotHaveParameter<T>, HasParameterCount, HasInParameter/HasOutParameter/HasRefParameter/HasOptionalParameter/HasParamsParameter), Has<TAttribute>. FluentAssertions aweXpect.Reflection typeof(Playlist).Should().HaveConstructor(new[] { typeof(int) }) .Which.Should().HaveAccessModifier(CSharpAccessModifier.Public); typeof(Playlist).Should().HaveDefaultConstructor(); await That(In.Type<Playlist>().Constructors().WhichArePublic()) .HaveParameterCount(1); await That(typeof(Playlist)).HasADefaultConstructor();

FluentAssertions: no FieldInfo assertions. aweXpect.Reflection: expectations on a single FieldInfo and on collections of fields, and an In.*…Fields() filter: IsStatic, IsReadOnly, IsConstant, IsRequired, IsNullable, IsOfType<T>/IsOfExactType<T> (and IsNotOfType<T>/IsNotOfExactType<T>), access modifiers (IsPublic, …), HasName, Has<TAttribute>. FluentAssertions aweXpect.Reflection // No dedicated FieldInfo assertions; fall back to raw reflection + LINQ/string assertions: typeof(Playlist).GetField("_tracks", BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic) .IsInitOnly.Should().BeTrue(); FieldInfo field = typeof(Playlist).GetField("_tracks", BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic); await That(field).IsReadOnly(); await That(field).IsPrivate(); await That(In.AssemblyContaining<Playlist>().Fields().WhichAreConstant()) .ArePublic();

FluentAssertions: no EventInfo assertions. aweXpect.Reflection: expectations on a single EventInfo and on collections of events, and an In.*…Events() filter: IsStatic, IsAbstract, IsSealed, IsOfType<T>/IsOfExactType<T> (and IsNotOfType<T>/IsNotOfExactType<T>), access modifiers, HasName, Has<TAttribute>. FluentAssertions aweXpect.Reflection // No dedicated EventInfo assertions; fall back to raw reflection: typeof(Playlist).GetEvent("Changed").Should().NotBeNull(); EventInfo @event = typeof(Playlist).GetEvent("Changed"); await That(@event).IsStatic(); await That(@event).Has<ObsoleteAttribute>(); await That(In.AssemblyContaining<Playlist>().Events().WhichArePublic()) .HaveName("Changed");

FluentAssertions: build a set with assembly.Types(), AllTypes.From(assembly), type.Methods(), type.Properties(), then narrow with selector methods (ThatAreClasses(), ThatDeriveFrom<T>(), ThatAreDecoratedWith<T>(), ThatAreInNamespace(), ThatReturn<T>(), ThatArePublicOrInternal, ThatSatisfy(predicate), …) and assert with the selector assertions. There are no FieldInfo/EventInfo selectors and no ConstructorInfo selector. aweXpect.Reflection: start from an In.* source, then chain WhichAre*/With<T>/WithName/Without* filters (with Or* combinations and quantifiers) across every member kind, and verify them with the plural Are*/Have* expectations. FluentAssertions aweXpect.Reflection AllTypes.From(assembly) .ThatAreClasses() .ThatAreDecoratedWith<TestFixtureAttribute>() .Should().BeInNamespace("MusicStore.Tests"); await That(In.AllLoadedAssemblies() .Methods().With<FactAttribute>().OrWith<TheoryAttribute>() .DeclaringTypes()) .HaveName("Tests").AsSuffix();

FluentAssertions: reflection assertions have no built-in name matching. Names are compared with the string API (type.Name.Should().StartWith(…)) or a LINQ predicate on a selector. aweXpect.Reflection: every name/namespace/dependency comparison exposes string options: AsPrefix(), AsSuffix(), AsRegex(), AsWildcard(), IgnoringCase(), Using(comparer). FluentAssertions aweXpect.Reflection type.Name.Should().EndWith("Tests"); await That(type).HasName("Tests").AsSuffix();

Set a value under Customize.aweXpect.Reflection() for the current async flow, or under Customize.aweXpect.Global.Reflection() for all tests. Value Default Summary Settings().ExcludedAssemblyPrefixes System, Microsoft, … assemblies excluded from In.AllLoadedAssemblies() and ignored by the DependOnlyOn family IncludedCompilerGeneratedMembers CompilerGeneratedMembers.None the compiler-generated types and members included in the navigations IncludedSpecialNameMembers SpecialNameMembers.None the operators and accessors included in .Methods() DependencyResolver built-in signature-level resolver how the type-level dependency expectations determine the dependencies of a type ExcludedAttributeTypes none additional compiler-emitted attributes that never count as dependencies Customize.aweXpect.Reflection() and the enums CompilerGeneratedMembers and SpecialNameMembers live in the namespace aweXpect.Reflection. The assembly exclusions are shared with aweXpect.Core and live under Customize.aweXpect.Settings(). For example, to include the operators in .Methods() for all tests: using aweXpect.Customization; using aweXpect.Reflection; Customize.aweXpect.Global.Reflection().IncludedSpecialNameMembers .Set(SpecialNameMembers.Operators);

By default, assemblies whose name matches one of the following prefixes are excluded from In.AllLoadedAssemblies(): mscorlib, System, Microsoft, netstandard, WindowsBase, JetBrains, xunit, Castle, DynamicProxyGenAssembly2. Both the assembly scanning and the dependency expectations (DependsOnlyOn / DependOnlyOn / WhichDependOnlyOn, on both assemblies and types) use the same prefixes with the same matching: a prefix matches at a name-segment boundary, so System covers System and System.Text.Json, but not an assembly named SystemsBiology. Customize this via Customize.aweXpect.Settings().ExcludedAssemblyPrefixes. Set(…) replaces the list: using (Customize.aweXpect.Settings().ExcludedAssemblyPrefixes .Set(new[] { "mscorlib", "System", "Microsoft", "MusicStore.Generated" })) { // In.AllLoadedAssemblies() applies the custom prefixes within this scope } Prefixes with a trailing dot A prefix written with a trailing dot (e.g. MusicStore.) is boundary-safe by construction and covers everything starting with it.

By default, compiler-generated types and members are excluded from every navigation (.Types(), .Methods(), .Fields(), …). This hides closures, async/iterator state machines, anonymous types, local functions, auto-property backing fields and the generated members of records (ToString, Equals, <Clone>$, the copy-constructor, …), so convention tests see only the members you actually wrote. Opt specific kinds back in with the [Flags] enum CompilerGeneratedMembers (None, Types, Constructors, Methods, Properties, Fields, Events, All): using (Customize.aweXpect.Reflection().IncludedCompilerGeneratedMembers .Set(CompilerGeneratedMembers.Types | CompilerGeneratedMembers.Methods)) { // closures, state machines and compiler-generated methods are now visible } Operators (op_*) and property/event accessors (get_, set_, add_, remove_) are user-written but likewise excluded by default. Include them via the separate SpecialNameMembers enum (None, Operators, Accessors, All), which only affects .Methods(): using (Customize.aweXpect.Reflection().IncludedSpecialNameMembers .Set(SpecialNameMembers.Operators)) { // operator methods are now visible in .Methods() }

The type-level dependency expectations compute a type's dependencies with a built-in signature-level resolver (base type, interfaces, field/property/event types, method/constructor signatures, generic arguments and applied attributes). Method-body references are not detected by the default; supply a custom resolver, e.g. backed by Mono.Cecil (this library takes no dependency on it; reference the package yourself), for IL/body-level accuracy: // Replace the resolver within a scope using (Customize.aweXpect.Reflection().DependencyResolver .Set(CecilDependencyResolver.GetUsedTypes)) { // the references in method bodies count as dependencies, too } // Or augment instead of replace: compose on the current default ICustomizationValueSetter<Func<Type, IEnumerable<Type>>?> resolver = Customize.aweXpect.Reflection().DependencyResolver; Func<Type, IEnumerable<Type>> builtin = resolver.Get()!; using (resolver.Set(type => builtin(type).Concat(CecilDependencyResolver.GetUsedTypes(type)))) { // the built-in dependencies plus the ones the Cecil resolver finds } // Setting null reverts to the built-in default, e.g. to opt a single test out // of a globally configured resolver using (Customize.aweXpect.Reflection().DependencyResolver.Set(null)) { // the signature-level default applies within this scope } Get() always returns the resolver currently in effect (the built-in default when none is configured), so composing on it works regardless of what an outer scope has set up. Example: a resolver backed by Mono.Cecil CecilDependencyResolver.GetUsedTypes reads a type with Mono.Cecil: its signature surface and the IL of its method bodies, i.e. the types of local variables, created or cast types, and the types of called methods and accessed fields. It reads the assembly file, so it skips an assembly that was loaded from memory or bundled into a single-file app. Code in lambdas, async methods and iterators is compiled into nested types, which are resolved as types of their own. using System.Collections.Generic; using Mono.Cecil; using Mono.Cecil.Cil; /// <summary> /// Example of a custom resolver for <c>Customize.aweXpect.Reflection().DependencyResolver</c>, backed by /// Mono.Cecil: in addition to the declared signature surface it reads method bodies from the IL, so /// references that only occur inside a body (object creations, static calls, locals) are detected as /// dependencies, too, which the built-in signature-level resolver cannot see. /// </summary> /// <remarks> /// The output does not need to be unwrapped, de-duplicated or cached here: the library normalizes and /// memoizes every resolver's output per type. /// </remarks> public static class CecilDependencyResolver { public static IEnumerable<Type> GetUsedTypes(Type type) { if (type.FullName is null || string.IsNullOrEmpty(type.Assembly.Location)) { yield break; } using AssemblyDefinition assembly = AssemblyDefinition.ReadAssembly(type.Assembly.Location); TypeDefinition? definition = assembly.MainModule.GetType(type.FullName.Replace('+', '/')); if (definition is null) { yield break; } foreach (TypeReference reference in EnumerateTypeReferences(definition)) { foreach (TypeReference flattened in Flatten(reference)) { if (ResolveRuntimeType(flattened) is { } resolved) { yield return resolved; } } } } private static IEnumerable<TypeReference> EnumerateTypeReferences(TypeDefinition definition) { if (definition.BaseType is not null) { yield return definition.BaseType; } foreach (InterfaceImplementation @interface in definition.Interfaces) { yield return @interface.InterfaceType; } foreach (FieldDefinition field in definition.Fields) { yield return field.FieldType; } foreach (PropertyDefinition property in definition.Properties) { yield return property.PropertyType; } foreach (EventDefinition @event in definition.Events) { yield return @event.EventType; } foreach (MethodDefinition method in definition.Methods) { yield return method.ReturnType; foreach (ParameterDefinition parameter in method.Parameters) { yield return parameter.ParameterType; } if (!method.HasBody) { continue; } foreach (VariableDefinition variable in method.Body.Variables) { yield return variable.VariableType; } foreach (Instruction instruction in method.Body.Instructions) { TypeReference? operandType = instruction.Operand switch { TypeReference typeReference => typeReference, MemberReference memberReference => memberReference.DeclaringType, _ => null, }; if (operandType is not null) { yield return operandType; } } } } /// <summary> /// Strips array/by-ref/pointer wrappers and flattens generic instances into their definition and /// arguments, so that every part can be resolved by full name. /// </summary> private static IEnumerable<TypeReference> Flatten(TypeReference reference) { while (reference is TypeSpecification specification and not GenericInstanceType) { reference = specification.ElementType; } if (reference is Mono.Cecil.GenericParameter) { yield break; } if (reference is GenericInstanceType generic) { yield return generic.ElementType; foreach (TypeReference argument in generic.GenericArguments) { foreach (TypeReference flattened in Flatten(argument)) { yield return flattened; } } } else { yield return reference; } } private static Type? ResolveRuntimeType(TypeReference reference) { string assemblyName = reference.Scope switch { AssemblyNameReference assemblyReference => assemblyReference.FullName, ModuleDefinition module => module.Assembly.FullName, _ => reference.Module.Assembly.FullName, }; return Type.GetType($"{reference.FullName.Replace('/', '+')}, {assemblyName}", false); } } The resolver must be pure Every resolver's output is normalized like the built-in's (array/by-ref/pointer element types and generic arguments are unwrapped, the result is de-duplicated) and cached per type for the lifetime of the resolver delegate, so a custom resolver needs no caching of its own. It must, however, be pure: deterministic for a given Type within its scope; that is what makes the caching safe.

A filter (.WhichAre… / .With…) narrows a collection before you verify it. An expectation (That(…).Is… / .Are… / .Has… / .Have…) states the rule the subject must satisfy. They mirror each other: a filter has an Is…/Are… expectation counterpart for the same concept.

The tables on the pages of this group pair them up. The Filter column is used on a selection (In.… or Types.…); the Expect (single) column applies to one subject; the Expect (many) column applies to a collection. The Negated column lists the negations in the same order (filter, single, many), leaving out a form that has none. An empty cell means that there is no such form, e.g. no negation.

Section Applies to Filters / expectations Access modifiers types and members WhichArePublic / IsPublic, WhichAre(AccessModifiers) / Is(AccessModifiers), … Attributes types, members and assemblies With<TAttribute> / Has<TAttribute>, Without<TAttribute> / DoesNotHave<TAttribute> Obsolete types and members WhichAreObsolete / IsObsolete, WhichAreNotObsolete / IsNotObsolete Names and namespaces types and members WithName / HasName, WithNamespace / HasNamespace, WhichAreWithinNamespace / IsWithinNamespace String matching options names and namespaces AsPrefix, AsSuffix, AsWildcard, AsRegex, IgnoringCase Assemblies assemblies WhichTarget / Targets, WithVersion / HasVersion, WhichDependOn / DependsOn Types types WhichAreClasses / IsAClass, WhichInheritFrom<T> / InheritsFrom<T>, WhichContainMethods / ContainsMethods Inheritance types and members Directly, IncludingInherited, IncludingObjectMembers Methods methods WhichAreAsync / IsAsync, WhichReturn<T> / Returns<T>, WithParameter<T> / HasParameter<T> Operators methods and types WhichAreOperators / IsAnOperator, WhichHaveOperator / HasOperator, WhichHaveImplicitConversionOperator Constructors constructors WithNoParameters / HasNoParameters, WithParameter<T> / HasParameter<T> Properties & Fields properties and fields WhichAreOfType<T> / IsOfType<T>, WhichAreNullable / IsNullable, WhichAreRequired / IsRequired Events events WhichAreOfType<T> / IsOfType<T>, WhichAreStatic / IsStatic, WhichAreNullable / IsNullable Combining filters filters and expectations OrWith<TAttribute> / OrHas<TAttribute>, OrReturn<T>, OrOfType<T> Custom predicates types, members and assemblies Which / Satisfies, Except Collections and quantifiers all subjects Satisfies, All().Satisfy, Any().Satisfy

Filters chain naturally (each narrows the previous result). Several filters offer an Or… companion to widen a single step. The attribute expectations have one as well: OrHas<TAttribute>() on a single subject and OrHave<TAttribute>() on a collection, both also with a predicate on the attribute: // Any of several attributes In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Methods() .With<FactAttribute>().OrWith<TheoryAttribute>() await That(method).Has<FactAttribute>().OrHas<TheoryAttribute>(); await That(methods).Have<FactAttribute>().OrHave<TheoryAttribute>(a => a.Skip == null); // Any of several return types In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Methods() .WhichReturn<Task>().OrReturn<ValueTask>() // Any of several property/field types In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Properties() .WhichAreOfType<string>().OrOfType<Guid>()

When no filter or expectation covers your rule, pass your own predicate. Like the other filters, they are available on every selection (assemblies, types and members): Filter Expect (single) Expect (many) Negated custom predicate .Which(x => …) .Satisfies(x => …) .All().Satisfy(x => …) / .Any().Satisfy(x => …) Except(x => …), Except<T>() (types only) The custom .Which(…) filter has a universal expectation counterpart that works for every subject kind (types, members and assemblies): use aweXpect's .Satisfies(…) on a single subject and .All().Satisfy(…) (or .Any().Satisfy(…)) on a collection. See Collections and quantifiers. The custom .Except(…) filter is the inverse of .Which(…): it removes the items that match the predicate. This is handy for defining exemptions to a rule (e.g. all async methods except this one). For types there is also a typed .Except<T>() overload that excludes exactly the type T. // Methods with a single parameter, except the event handlers In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Methods() .Which(method => method.GetParameters().Length == 1) .Except(method => method.Name.StartsWith("On")) // All types of the album assembly, except one legacy type In.AssemblyContaining<Album>().Types().Except<LegacyImportService>()

Every expectation works with both a single item and a collection. A collection can be an array, any IEnumerable<T?> or, on .NET 8 and later, an IAsyncEnumerable<T?>. The plural expectations already require every item to match; for ad-hoc predicates use aweXpect's Satisfies(…) (single subject) and All() / Any() quantifiers with Satisfy(…) (collections), and combine selections with LINQ: // The plural expectation already means "every item": await That(types).ArePublic(); // Ad-hoc predicate on a single subject: await That(type).Satisfies(type => type.IsSealed); // Ad-hoc predicate across the whole collection: await That(types).All().Satisfy(type => type.IsSealed); await That(types).Any().Satisfy(type => type.IsAbstract); // Mix with LINQ (assign to IEnumerable<Type?> so Where binds to LINQ): IEnumerable<Type?> publicClasses = In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Types() .WhichAreClasses().WhichArePublic(); IEnumerable<Type?> managers = publicClasses.Where(type => type!.GetInterfaces().Length > 2); await That(managers).HaveName("Manager").AsSuffix(); The plural expectations that only check a condition on each item, like AreSealed(), AreNotStatic(), HaveADefaultConstructor() or HaveNamespace(…), read the whole collection and list every item that violates them. They also follow aweXpect's quantifiers, which only read the items until the outcome is determined, and keep their string options: await That(types).AtLeast(2).AreSealed(); await That(methods).AtMost(1).AreAsync(); await That(types).AtLeast(2).HaveNamespace("MusicStore").AsPrefix(); The same holds for the relations, operators, generic arguments and members of types: InheritFrom, Implement, AreGeneric, HaveOperator, HaveImplicitConversionOperator, HaveExplicitConversionOperator, OnlyHaveNullableMembers, OnlyHaveNonNullableMembers and the Contain… checks. They keep their options, like Directly(), and their negations mean that no item matches (none inherit from MediaItem): await That(types).AtLeast(2).InheritFrom<MediaItem>().Directly(); await That(types).None().Implement<IDisposable>(); await That(types).AtMost(1).ContainMethods(methods => methods.With<ObsoleteAttribute>()); The parameter and return type expectations of methods and constructors take quantifiers as well: HaveParameter, HaveParameterExactly and their ref / out / in / params / optional variants, HaveParameterCount, HaveNoParameters, Return, ReturnExactly, ReturnVoid and AreGeneric on methods. Their options, like AtIndex(…) or OrReturn<T>(), apply to each item, and their negations, like DoNotHaveParameter<bool>(), read none have parameter of type bool: await That(methods).AtLeast(2).HaveParameter<CancellationToken>().AtIndexFromEnd(0); await That(methods).None().Return<Task>().OrReturn<ValueTask>(); await That(constructors).AtMost(1).HaveNoParameters(); The attribute expectations Have<TAttribute>() on types, members and assemblies and the type expectations AreOfType<T>() and AreOfExactType<T>() on properties, fields and events take quantifiers as well and keep OrHave…, OrOfType… and Directly(). Their negations DoNotHave<TAttribute>(), AreNotOfType<T>() and AreNotOfExactType<T>() mean that no item matches (none have ObsoleteAttribute): await That(methods).AtLeast(1).Have<FactAttribute>().OrHave<TheoryAttribute>(); await That(properties).None().AreOfType<DateTime>(); On a struct collection, such as an ImmutableArray<Type>, pass the type as an argument after a quantifier, e.g. AtLeast(2).InheritFrom(typeof(MediaItem)), as C# cannot infer the collection type next to an explicit type argument.

Assemblies are usually used as a source, but you can also filter and verify them directly. Filters and expectations explains how to read the tables. Filter Expect (single) Expect (many) Negated by name .WithName("x") .HasName("x") .HaveName("x") WithoutName, DoesNotHaveName, DoNotHaveName by target framework .WhichTarget("net8.0") .Targets("net8.0") .Target("net8.0") WhichDoNotTarget, DoesNotTarget, DoNotTarget by version .WithVersion(…) .HasVersion(…) .HaveVersion(…) strong named .WhichAreStrongNamed() .IsStrongNamed() .AreStrongNamed() WhichAreNotStrongNamed, IsNotStrongNamed, AreNotStrongNamed has attribute .With<TAttribute>() .Has<TAttribute>() .Have<TAttribute>() Without<TAttribute>, DoesNotHave<TAttribute>, DoNotHave<TAttribute> depends on assembly .WhichDependOn("x") .DependsOn("x") .DependOn("x") WhichDoNotDependOn, DoesNotDependOn, DoNotDependOn depends only on set .WhichDependOnlyOn("x", …) .DependsOnlyOn("x", …) .DependOnlyOn("x", …) custom predicate .Which(a => …) .Satisfies(a => …) .All().Satisfy(a => …) Except(a => …) Assembly subject = Assembly.GetEntryAssembly(); Assembly[] subjects = AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies(); await That(subject).HasName("MusicStore").AsPrefix(); await That(subject).DependsOn("System.Core"); await That(subject).DoesNotDependOn("UnwantedDependency"); await That(subject).DependsOnlyOn("MusicStore.Domain"); await That(subjects).Have<AssemblyTitleAttribute>(); await That(subject).Targets("net8.0"); The target framework is matched against the short moniker form (e.g. net8.0, netstandard2.0, net48), derived from the assembly's [TargetFramework] attribute. The negations WhichDoNotTarget / DoesNotTarget / DoNotTarget accept the same string matching options, and DoNotTarget verifies that none of the assemblies targets the framework. An assembly is considered strong named when its name carries a non-empty public key token. The version filter and expectations come in two forms. Pass a Func<Version, bool> predicate to match the whole version, or omit it to compare individual components (WithMajor, WithMinor, WithBuild, WithRevision). The filter and the expectations compare a component with the same operators as the int properties of core aweXpect, e.g. HasLength(): EqualTo, GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEqualTo, LessThan, LessThanOrEqualTo, Between(…).And(…) and their negations NotEqualTo, NotGreaterThan, NotBetween(…).And(…), and so on. Component comparisons chain (all must hold). // Predicate form In.AllLoadedAssemblies().WithVersion(version => version.Major >= 2) await That(subject).HasVersion(version => version.Major >= 2); // Component form In.AllLoadedAssemblies().WithVersion().WithMajor.GreaterThanOrEqualTo(2).WithMinor.EqualTo(0) In.AllLoadedAssemblies().WithVersion().WithMajor.Between(2).And(4).WithMinor.NotLessThan(1) await That(subject).HasVersion().WithMajor.GreaterThanOrEqualTo(2); await That(subjects).HaveVersion().WithMajor.EqualTo(1); await That(subject).HasVersion().WithMajor.Between(2).And(4).WithMinor.NotEqualTo(0); On a collection of assemblies, HaveVersion and DependOnlyOn also follow aweXpect's quantifiers: await That(subjects).AtLeast(2).HaveVersion().WithMajor.EqualTo(1); await That(subjects).AtLeast(2).DependOnlyOn("MusicStore.Domain"); Assemblies without a target framework or version Assemblies without a [TargetFramework] attribute are treated as having no target framework and never match. An assembly without a version never matches a version filter or expectation. The Build and Revision components are -1 when absent from the version.

Combined flags are met by any of them, e.g. AccessModifiers.Public | AccessModifiers.Internal reads "is public or internal", and AccessModifiers.Any is met by every type and member. [Test] [Arguments(AccessModifiers.Public)] [Arguments(AccessModifiers.Public | AccessModifiers.Internal)] public async Task TypesAreNotNested(AccessModifiers modifier) { await That(In.AssemblyContaining<PlaylistService>().Types().WhichAre(modifier)) .AreNotNested(); } [Test] [Arguments(typeof(PlaylistService), AccessModifiers.Public)] [Arguments(typeof(TrackCache), AccessModifiers.Internal)] public async Task TypeHasTheExpectedAccessModifier(Type type, AccessModifiers modifier) { await That(type).Is(modifier); } await That(methods).AreNot(AccessModifiers.Private | AccessModifiers.PrivateProtected);

Shared by all types and members. Filter Expect (single) Expect (many) Negated by name .WithName("x") .HasName("x") .HaveName("x") WithoutName, DoesNotHaveName, DoNotHaveName by namespace (types only) .WithNamespace("x") .HasNamespace("x") .HaveNamespace("x") WithoutNamespace, DoesNotHaveNamespace, DoNotHaveNamespace within namespace (types only) .WhichAreWithinNamespace("x") .IsWithinNamespace("x") .AreWithinNamespace("x") WhichAreNotWithinNamespace, IsNotWithinNamespace, AreNotWithinNamespace The negated filter keeps the items whose name does not match, the single expectation verifies an item is not named the given value, and the collection expectation verifies that none of the items are; the same holds for the namespace of types. They accept the same string matching options as their positive counterparts: // Verify that no type in the production assembly is named with a "Test" suffix await That(In.AssemblyContaining<PlaylistService>().Types()) .DoNotHaveName("Test").AsSuffix(); The name/namespace equality filters and expectations (WithName, WithNamespace, and their Has/Have counterparts) accept the string matching options (AsPrefix, AsSuffix, AsWildcard, AsRegex, IgnoringCase, …). Collection expectations also accept a selector to derive the expected name per item, also after a quantifier: await That(types).HaveName("Service").AsSuffix(); await That(methods).HaveName(m => "On" + m.GetParameters()[0].ParameterType.Name); await That(methods).AtLeast(1).HaveName(m => "Get" + m.ReturnType.Name); The WhichAreWithinNamespace/IsWithinNamespace/AreWithinNamespace variants match a namespace and all its sub-namespaces (so MusicStore.Data includes MusicStore.Data.Sql but not MusicStore.DataImport). They compare the namespace exactly and case-sensitively. Their negations match types outside the namespace. Unlike DoesNotHaveNamespace, which compares the whole namespace as a string with the string matching options, IsNotWithinNamespace also excludes all sub-namespaces.

Every filter and expectation that compares a name, a namespace, a target framework or a dependency, including the parameter and generic argument names, uses the string matching options of the core aweXpect library (see the string options, the match types and the general option rules): Option Effect (none) exact match (default) .AsPrefix() the value must start with the expected string .AsSuffix() the value must end with the expected string .AsWildcard() match using * and ? wildcards .AsRegex() / .AsRegex(regexOptions) match using a regular expression .IgnoringCase() case-insensitive comparison .IgnoringLeadingWhiteSpace() / .IgnoringTrailingWhiteSpace() trim before comparing .NormalizingWhiteSpace() collapse runs of whitespace before comparing .Using(comparer) compare with a custom IEqualityComparer<string> await That(types).HaveName("Service").AsSuffix(); await That(types).HaveName("*Test*").AsWildcard(); await That(types).HaveName(@"^Test\w+$").AsRegex(); await That(methods).HaveName("Get*Async").AsWildcard().IgnoringCase(); Filtered.Types services = In.AssemblyContaining<PlaylistService>().Types() .WithName("service").IgnoringCase().AsSuffix() .WhichAreClasses();

They have no Or… companion: chain .WhichDoNotReturn<T1>().WhichDoNotReturn<T2>() (or combine expectations with .And) to exclude several return types. // Async methods never return void await That(In.AssemblyContaining<PlaylistService>().Methods().WhichAreAsync()) .DoNotReturnVoid(); The ref / out / in / params / optional parameter filters and expectations mirror WithParameter: each also has <T>(), (Type), <T>("name") and …Exactly<T>() overloads to constrain the parameter's type and name (e.g. .WithRefParameter<int>("count"), .HasOutParameterExactly<string>()). The parameter filters and expectations (WithParameter, HasParameter, HaveParameter and their variants) take these options to narrow down the parameter; they combine, and all of them must hold for the same parameter: Option Effect .AtIndex(n) the parameter at the zero-based index n .AtIndexFromEnd(n) the parameter at the zero-based index n, counted from the last parameter .WithDefaultValue() a parameter with a default value .WithDefaultValue(value) a parameter with the default value value .WithoutDefaultValue() a parameter without a default value .WithRefModifier() (filters only) a ref parameter .WithOutModifier() (filters only) an out parameter .WithInModifier() (filters only) an in parameter .WithOptionalModifier() (filters only) an optional parameter .WithParamsModifier() (filters only) a params parameter .Matching(p => …) a parameter matching the predicate on its ParameterInfo WithoutParameter / DoesNotHaveParameter / DoNotHaveParameter are the negations of WithParameter / HasParameter / HaveParameter, with the <T>(), (Type), <T>("name"), (Type, "name") and ("name") overloads and the same options (AtIndex(…), AtIndexFromEnd(…), WithDefaultValue(…), the string matching options for the name and, on the filter, the modifiers like WithRefModifier()). They match when no parameter satisfies all of them, and DoNotHaveParameter verifies that for every item of a collection. It is available on every parameter filter and expectation, including the negations and the parameterless ref / out / in / params / optional variants, and combines with the other options. WithParamsParameter() matches params arrays and C# 13 params collections alike; Matching tells them apart: // Consumers below C# 13 cannot pass single values to a params collection await That(In.AssemblyContaining<PlaylistService>().Public.Methods() .WithParamsParameter().Matching(p => !p.ParameterType.IsArray)) .IsEmpty(); WhichAreExtensionMethods(), IsAnExtensionMethod() and AreExtensionMethods() match both classic this-parameter extension methods and extension methods declared with the C# extension block syntax (extension(...) { … }), including static extension methods. In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Methods() .WhichArePublic() .WhichReturn<Task>().OrReturn<ValueTask>() .WithParameter<CancellationToken>() .With<HttpGetAttribute>().OrWith<HttpPostAttribute>() await That(method).HasParameter<int>("count"); await That(methods).Return<Task>().OrReturn<ValueTask>(); Extension block internals The compiler-generated grouping types backing the extension block syntax are excluded from the reflected members.

The Operator enum maps each C# operator to its compiler-emitted op_* metadata name (e.g. Operator.Addition ↔ op_Addition), so operator expectations are type-safe and discoverable instead of relying on magic strings. It covers unary, binary, comparison and conversion operators, including the C# 11 checked variants and >>> (UnsignedRightShift). Scope Filter Expect (single) Expect (many) Negated any operator method .WhichAreOperators() .IsAnOperator() .AreOperators() WhichAreNotOperators, IsNotAnOperator, AreNotOperators specific operator .WhichAreOperators(Operator) .IsAnOperator(Operator) .AreOperators(Operator) WhichAreNotOperators(Operator), IsNotAnOperator(Operator), AreNotOperators(Operator) type has operator .WhichHaveOperator(Operator) .HasOperator(Operator) .HaveOperator(Operator) WhichDoNotHaveOperator(Operator), DoesNotHaveOperator(Operator), DoNotHaveOperator(Operator) implicit conversion .WhichHaveImplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>() .HasImplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>() .HaveImplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>() WhichDoNotHaveImplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>, DoesNotHaveImplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>, DoNotHaveImplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget> explicit conversion .WhichHaveExplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>() .HasExplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>() .HaveExplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>() WhichDoNotHaveExplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>, DoesNotHaveExplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget>, DoNotHaveExplicitConversionOperator<TSource, TTarget> // Method-level: narrow an operator method to a specific operator await That(methodInfo).IsAnOperator(Operator.Equality); await That(methods).AreOperators(Operator.Equality); // Type-level presence (op_* lookup), including the operators of base types await That(typeof(TrackDuration)).HasOperator(Operator.Addition); await That(typeof(TrackDuration)).HasOperator(Operator.Subtraction).Directly(); await That(typeof(TrackDuration)).DoesNotHaveOperator(Operator.Modulus); // Disambiguate overloads by operand type await That(typeof(TrackDuration)).HasOperator<int>(Operator.Addition); // Conversion operators are keyed by their source → target signature await That(typeof(TrackDuration)).HasImplicitConversionOperator<TrackDuration, TimeSpan>(); await That(typeof(TrackDuration)).HasExplicitConversionOperator(typeof(TrackDuration), typeof(int)); // Filter for the types that declare an operator themselves In.AssemblyContaining<TrackDuration>().Types().WhichHaveOperator(Operator.Addition).Directly() WhichHaveOperator / HasOperator and the conversion operator filters and expectations also match the operators inherited from base types; append .Directly() to only match the operators declared on the type itself. Conversion source/target types are matched exactly. The filters, the expectations and their negations also come with the operand overloads, e.g. WhichHaveOperator<int>(Operator) or DoesNotHaveOperator<int>(Operator). Operators are hidden by default Operators are special-name members that are hidden by default, so the plain .Methods() collection excludes them unless opted in via IncludedSpecialNameMembers. The .WhichAreOperators(Operator) filter implicitly re-includes operators for its query, so it works without that configuration. The negative .WhichAreNotOperators(Operator) filter does not re-include operators; if you want the other operators in that result, opt in via IncludedSpecialNameMembers. Why WhichAreNotOperators does not re-include operators A "not this operator" filter over .Methods() is meant to narrow regular methods, and force-including every other operator would surprise more than help.

A property or field counts as nullable when its type is a Nullable<T> value type (e.g. int?) or a reference type annotated as nullable (e.g. string?, based on the nullable reference type metadata emitted by the compiler). The same applies to events, whose handler type is always a delegate (reference) type. // All properties and fields of the request types must be nullable await That(In.AssemblyContaining<AddTrackRequest>() .Types().WithName("Request").AsSuffix() .Properties()) .AreNullable(); Nullability and extension properties in detail The nullability check follows the declared annotation on every target framework: reference types without nullability annotations (oblivious code compiled without <Nullable>enable</Nullable>) and unconstrained generic type parameters (T, as opposed to T?) count as non-nullable, and post-condition attributes like [AllowNull] or [MaybeNull] are ignored. The real extension properties live on the compiler-generated grouping types backing the extension block, so they are surfaced from there, while the public accessor methods they emit are excluded from the reflected methods.

argument or a Type. Append .Directly() to require the base class to be the direct parent. For interfaces, use Implements. WhichImplement / Implements consider only implemented interfaces. With .Directly(), an interface reached only through a base class or through another implemented interface does not count as directly implemented. The negations accept .Directly() as well (e.g. WhichDoNotInheritFrom<T>().Directly(), DoesNotImplement<T>().Directly()). Inheritance shows samples. IsAssignableTo / IsAssignableFrom (and their WhichAre… / Are… forms) use runtime assignability, which covers base classes and interfaces in one step, treats a type as assignable to itself, and honors closed generic variance. In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Types() .WhichAreClasses().WhichArePublic() .WithName("Service").AsSuffix() .WhichInheritFrom<BaseService>() // Shorthand for the same access/kind filters In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Public.Abstract.Classes() A type is instantiable when it is a concrete type that is neither abstract, static nor an interface, and not an open generic type definition. Default constructor checks for an accessible parameterless constructor (value types always have one); this is independent of instantiability (e.g. a type with only a parameterized constructor is instantiable but has no default constructor). A type is immutable when all instance fields (including inherited ones) are readonly and all instance properties (including inherited ones) have no setter or an init-only setter. Static members do not affect immutability. Failure messages list the offending mutable members for actionable feedback. OnlyHasNullableMembers / OnlyHaveNullableMembers (and the non-nullable counterparts) verify the nullability of all fields, properties and events of the type, including the inherited ones unless .Directly() is appended; the failure message lists the non-compliant members per type: await That(In.AssemblyContaining<AddTrackRequest>() .Types().WithName("Request").AsSuffix()) .OnlyHaveNullableMembers();

You can select types based on their members. The lambda receives the members of each individual type, including the inherited ones unless .Directly() is appended (see Inheritance), and may use the full member-filter API: // Types that contain at least one method with [Fact] or [Theory] In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Types() .WhichContainMethods(methods => methods.With<FactAttribute>().OrWith<TheoryAttribute>()) // The same is available for the other member kinds In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Types() .WhichContainProperties(properties => properties.With<RequiredAttribute>()) .WhichContainFields(fields => fields.WithName("_").AsPrefix()) .WhichContainEvents(events => events.With<ObsoleteAttribute>()) .WhichContainConstructors(constructors => constructors.WithNoParameters()) By default a type matches when it contains at least one matching member. Append a quantifier (the same quantifiers as in aweXpect) to require a specific count: In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Types() .WhichContainConstructors(c => c.WithNoParameters()).Exactly(1) .WhichContainMethods(m => m.With<ObsoleteAttribute>()).Never() .WhichContainProperties(p => p.With<RequiredAttribute>()).AtLeast(2) .WhichContainFields(f => f.WhichArePrivate()).Between(1).And(5) Each quantifier applies only to the condition it directly follows; all other conditions implicitly require the member to occur at least once. The available quantifiers are Exactly, AtLeast, AtMost, MoreThan, LessThan, Between(…).And(…), Never, Once and Twice. The counts are plain int values, both on filters and on expectations. The same five member kinds are available as expectations on a single Type (Contains…) and on a collection of types (Contain…), using the same member-filter lambdas and the same quantifiers (default: at least one matching member): Member kind Filter Expect (single) Expect (many) Negated methods .WhichContainMethods(…) .ContainsMethods(…) .ContainMethods(…) use .Never() properties .WhichContainProperties(…) .ContainsProperties(…) .ContainProperties(…) use .Never() fields .WhichContainFields(…) .ContainsFields(…) .ContainFields(…) use .Never() events .WhichContainEvents(…) .ContainsEvents(…) .ContainEvents(…) use .Never() constructors .WhichContainConstructors(…) .ContainsConstructors(…) .ContainConstructors(…) use .Never() // A single type contains at least one [Fact] or [Theory] method await That(typeof(PlaylistServiceTests)) .ContainsMethods(methods => methods.With<FactAttribute>().OrWith<TheoryAttribute>()); // …with exactly one parameterless constructor await That(typeof(PlaylistService)) .ContainsConstructors(constructors => constructors.WithNoParameters()).Exactly(1); // Every type in a collection contains a matching property await That(types) .ContainProperties(properties => properties.With<RequiredAttribute>()).AtLeast(1);

After .WhichAreGeneric() you can drill into the generic arguments themselves. The same filters are available on generic methods (.Methods().WhichAreGeneric()). Filter Selects generic types/methods… .WithArgumentCount(n) with exactly n generic arguments .WithArgument<T>() with a generic argument constrained to T .WithArgument<T>("name") with a generic argument constrained to T and named "name" .WithArgument("name") with a generic argument named "name" .AtIndex(n) / .AtIndexFromEnd(n) restrict the preceding WithArgument to a position (optionally counted from the end) The "name" overloads accept the string matching options, and .AtIndex(n) or .AtIndexFromEnd(n) is chained after a WithArgument to pin it to a specific position. // Generic types with a single argument constrained to IEntity In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Types() .WhichAreGeneric().WithArgumentCount(1).WithArgument<IEntity>() // Generic methods whose first argument is named "TKey" In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Methods() .WhichAreGeneric().WithArgument("TKey").AtIndex(0)

A check on a type considers what the type inherits: inherited attributes, operators, members and relations count by default, and .Directly() restricts the check to what is declared on the item itself, or to a direct relation. Listing the members of types (Types().Methods(), …) only includes the members declared on each type, as an inherited member would otherwise be listed once for each type that inherits it; .IncludingInherited() adds the inherited members. The members declared on System.Object, System.ValueType and System.Enum are excluded, as every type would otherwise have ToString, Equals, GetHashCode, …; .IncludingObjectMembers() adds them. Area Default Options Attributes of types, methods, properties and events also the attributes inherited from a base type or an overridden member .Directly(): only the attributes declared on the item Operators and conversion operators of types also the operators of base types .Directly(): only the operators declared on the type Relations (InheritsFrom<T>(), Implements<T>(), their filters and negations) the base class anywhere in the base-class chain, or any implemented interface .Directly(): only the direct base class or a directly implemented interface Member checks (ContainsMethods(…), WhichContainMethods(…), OnlyHasNullableMembers(), …) also the inherited members .Directly(): only the declared members, or .IncludingObjectMembers(): also the members of the three roots Member listings of types (Types().Methods(), In.Type<T>().Properties(), …) only the declared members .IncludingInherited(): also the inherited members, .IncludingObjectMembers(): also those of the three roots Member listings of assemblies (In.AssemblyContaining<T>().Methods(), …) each member once, on the type that declares it Constructors, and the attributes of assemblies, constructors and fields no inheritance await That(typeof(AlbumController)).InheritsFrom<ControllerBase>().Directly(); await That(typeof(AlbumRepository)).Implements<IRepository>().Directly(); await That(typeof(TrackDuration)).HasOperator(Operator.Addition).Directly(); await That(typeof(Album)).Has<SerializableAttribute>().Directly(); await That(typeof(Album)).ContainsMethods(methods => methods.WithName("Play")).Directly(); // The declared methods of the album types, also the inherited ones, and also those of System.Object await That(In.AssemblyContaining<Album>().Types().Methods()).AreNotObsolete(); await That(In.AssemblyContaining<Album>().Types().Methods().IncludingInherited()).AreNotObsolete(); await That(In.AssemblyContaining<Album>().Types().Methods().IncludingObjectMembers()).AreNotObsolete(); The options apply to the whole result, e.g. to all attributes of .With<T1>().OrWith<T2>().Directly(). On a member listing, set them directly after selecting the members, e.g. Types().Methods().IncludingInherited().WhichArePublic(). Inherited members in detail Inherited members never include those a derived type cannot access: the private members of base types and the internal members of base types in another assembly (InternalsVisibleTo is not considered). Only the immutability check considers all fields and properties of base types, including those a derived type cannot access, as they hold the state of an instance. An interface inherits the members of its base interfaces. On a member check, .Directly() and .IncludingObjectMembers() exclude each other, so only one of them can be set. On the WhichContain… filters, set them before or after the quantifier. Inside a member check, .Directly() on an attribute filter only restricts the attributes: in ContainsMethods(m => m.With<FactAttribute>().Directly()) the method may still be inherited.

Every expectation starts from a selection: the assemblies, types or members the rule applies to. This page covers the two entry points (In and Types) and navigating between assemblies, types and members.

In builds the collection of reflection objects you want to reason about. Every source returns a lazily evaluated collection that you can navigate and filter further. Source Returns In.AllLoadedAssemblies() all currently loaded assemblies (system assemblies excluded) In.Assemblies(a1, a2, …) / In.Assemblies(collection) the given assemblies In.AssemblyContaining<T>() / In.AssemblyContaining(typeof(T)) the assembly that declares T In.Type<T>() / In.Type(typeof(T)) a single type In.Types<T1, T2>() / In.Types<T1, T2, T3>() / In.Types(t1, t2, …) the given types In.Constructors(…) / In.Events(…) / In.Fields(…) / In.Methods(…) / In.Properties(…) the given members When a source is evaluated A source is read each time an expectation enumerates it, not when it is created: a source stored in a field also sees assemblies loaded later and the assembly exclusions customized at that time, and a collection you pass in is enumerated again on every evaluation.

While In starts from concrete reflection objects, Types selects types by criteria, the natural entry point for architecture rules: Source Returns Types.InNamespace("ns") all types within a namespace and its sub-namespaces (across loaded assemblies) Types.InAllLoadedAssemblies() all types in all currently loaded assemblies Types.InAssemblies(a1, a2, …) all types in the given assemblies Types.InAssemblyContaining<T>() / …(typeof(T)) all types in the assembly that declares T Types.InNamespace(…) searches all loaded assemblies by default; chain one of the same In* methods directly after it to clarify the assembly source: // Defaults to all loaded assemblies await That(Types.InNamespace("MusicStore.Domain")).AreSealed(); // Clarify the assembly source await That(Types.InNamespace("MusicStore.Domain").InAssemblyContaining<MusicStore.Startup>()) .AreSealed();

From a collection of assemblies or types you can navigate to the members they contain, and from members back to their declaring types. From Navigate with Yields assemblies .Types() the contained types assemblies / types .Methods(), .Properties(), .Fields(), .Events(), .Constructors() the contained members members .DeclaringTypes() the declaring types types .Assemblies() the declaring assemblies Assemblies also expose shorthand terminals that select a type kind directly: .Classes(), .Interfaces(), .Enums(), .Structs(), .Records(), .RecordStructs(). // All types in all (non-system) assemblies In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Types() // Navigate from members back to their declaring types In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Methods().DeclaringTypes() // Shorthand: all public classes In.AllLoadedAssemblies().Public.Classes()

aweXpect.Snapshots extends aweXpect with snapshot tests: it compares strings and objects with reviewed snapshots, which are stored next to the tests or in a store of your own, e.g. to verify generated text or a complex result without writing out the expected value.

.NET CLI PackageReference Central Package Management dotnet add package aweXpect.Snapshots --prerelease <PackageReference Include="aweXpect.Snapshots" Version="4.0.0-beta.0.pre.3" /> Directory.Packages.props <PackageVersion Include="aweXpect.Snapshots" Version="4.0.0-beta.0.pre.3" /> Project file <PackageReference Include="aweXpect.Snapshots" /> Latest version: 4.0.0-beta.0.pre.3 aweXpect.Snapshots: MatchesSnapshot for strings, objects, binary data and files. The other two packages bring it with them. aweXpect.Snapshots.DiffEngine: add it to open a diff tool for a missing or different snapshot when the tests run locally; it registers itself, see Diff tools. aweXpect.Snapshots.PublicApi: add it to verify the public API of an assembly with MatchesPublicApiSnapshot, see Public API. The packages bring Expect.That with them, but not the expectations for strings, numbers or collections, so reference aweXpect as well. MatchesSnapshot and MatchesPublicApiSnapshot live in the namespace aweXpect; OrphanedSnapshots, SnapshotAcceptance, SnapshotRule and the customization need using aweXpect.Snapshots;. The examples write That(...) instead of Expect.That(...), which needs using static aweXpect.Expect; (see Getting started).

// compare a string with the snapshot that is stored next to the test await That(description).MatchesSnapshot(); // compare an object, written completely and indented by the aweXpect formatter await That(album).MatchesSnapshot(); // compare an exception member-wise, without members that vary per build or machine, like the stack trace await That(() => player.Play(album, -1)).Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>().Which.MatchesSnapshot(); // replace values that change from run to run before comparing await That(playlist).MatchesSnapshot().For.Text(@"plays=\d+").AsRegex().Mask("plays=<count>"); // replace every Guid and ISO 8601 date with a numbered placeholder ({Guid_1}, {Date_1}, …) await That(playlist).MatchesSnapshot().For.Guids().Mask().For.Dates().Mask(); // leave out, mask or convert members of an object, selected by their name, type or declaring type await That(album).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Members().WithName("PlayCount").Ignore() .For.Members().WithName("Id").Mask() .For.Members().DeclaredIn<Album>().WithName("Released").OfType<DateTime>().Convert(date => date.Year); // store a JSON string as AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.json for syntax highlighting await That(json).MatchesSnapshot().WithExtension("json"); // keep a snapshot per target framework and operating system // (AlbumTests.Describes@net8.0@windows.awexpect-snapshot.txt) await That(exception.Message).MatchesSnapshot() .UniqueFor.TargetFramework().UniqueFor.OperatingSystem(); // verify the public API of an assembly, written as C# declarations // (package aweXpect.Snapshots.PublicApi) await That(typeof(Album).Assembly).MatchesPublicApiSnapshot() .UniqueFor.TargetFramework(); The snapshot is stored as <TestFile>.<Method>.awexpect-snapshot.txt next to the test file, where <TestFile> is the name of the test file without its extension. A missing or different snapshot fails the test and writes the actual value to <TestFile>.<Method>.awexpect-snapshot.pending.txt; rename it to <TestFile>.<Method>.awexpect-snapshot.txt to accept it, or set the environment variable AWEXPECT_ACCEPT_SNAPSHOTS to all to accept all changed snapshots of a test run (or to new to only add the missing ones). Before the first run, the snapshot of description does not exist yet, so the expectation fails with: Failure message Expected that description matches the snapshot "/src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.txt", but the snapshot did not exist Actual: Abbey Road by The Beatles Pending snapshot: /src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.pending.txt

Expectations for string and any other object: Expectation Negated Summary MatchesSnapshot a string matches the snapshot stored next to the test, with rules for its lines and text MatchesSnapshot an object matches its snapshot, written by aweXpect, with rules for its members and text Expectations for Assembly and FileInfo, from aweXpect.Snapshots.PublicApi: Expectation Negated Summary MatchesPublicApiSnapshot the public API of the assembly, or of the assembly in the file, matches the snapshot

Set a value under Customize.aweXpect.Snapshots() for the current async flow, or under Customize.aweXpect.Global.Snapshots() for all tests. Value Default Summary Acceptance null, left to the variable AWEXPECT_ACCEPT_SNAPSHOTS which missing or changed snapshots are accepted Rules none the rules to mask or ignore values in every snapshot Store a file next to the test file where the snapshots are kept Comparers none decide whether a value matches its snapshot, e.g. for images Reporters none are told about every missing, different or matching snapshot NamedAfterTestArguments false names each snapshot after the arguments of the test case AttachPendingFiles false attaches the pending file of a mismatch to the test result

Matching snapshots: strings, objects, exceptions, binary data and files, the file extension, encoding and line breaks Accepting snapshots: reviewing the pending file, accepting all changes of a run and attaching the pending files on a build server Diff tools: open a diff tool for a missing or different snapshot with DiffEngine, in which the change can be taken over into the snapshot Naming snapshots: a snapshot per test case or environment, and nested under their test file in Rider and Visual Studio Masking and ignoring values: mask, convert or leave out values that change from run to run Orphaned snapshots: OrphanedSnapshots.CheckAsync() in the teardown of the test run reports the snapshots that no test uses any more on a build server, and deletes them while accepting all changes Public API: MatchesPublicApiSnapshot from aweXpect.Snapshots.PublicApi Advanced: Storing snapshots elsewhere: a SnapshotStore instead of files next to the tests, e.g. a shared folder or a database Comparers: decide whether a value matches its snapshot instead of the built-in comparison, e.g. an image comparer that tolerates small differences of single pixels Reporters: are told about every missing, different or matching snapshot, e.g. to open a diff tool Deterministic builds: how the snapshots are found when the build replaces the path of the repository with /_/

A missing or different snapshot writes the actual value to <TestFile>.<Method>.awexpect-snapshot.pending.txt next to the snapshot. Review it and rename it to <TestFile>.<Method>.awexpect-snapshot.txt to accept it. The next run that matches the snapshot deletes a leftover pending file. Add the pending files to your .gitignore, so that they are not committed by accident; the pattern also covers snapshots with another extension, e.g. .awexpect-snapshot.pending.json: .gitignore *.awexpect-snapshot.pending.* To accept many snapshots at once, set the environment variable AWEXPECT_ACCEPT_SNAPSHOTS to one of the levels of SnapshotAcceptance and run the tests: Level Variable A missing snapshot A different snapshot None none, 0 or false writes the pending file writes the pending file New new is accepted writes the pending file All all, 1 or true is accepted is accepted An empty or unset variable accepts nothing. New adds the snapshots of new tests without touching the reviewed ones. An accepted snapshot is replaced by the actual value, and the expectation still fails, so that it never goes unnoticed: Failure message Expected that description matches the snapshot "/src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.txt", but the snapshot did not exist Actual: Abbey Road by The Beatles Accepted snapshot: /src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.txt The next run compares with the accepted snapshot. Review the changed snapshots in version control before committing them. Snapshots combined with other expectations The pending snapshot is only written, and a change only accepted, when the whole expectation fails. When the snapshot is combined with other expectations and another branch is met, e.g. .Or.IsEqualTo(…) or Expect.ThatAny(…), the test passes and nothing is written, so that a passing test never changes a snapshot.

The environment variable is ignored on a build server (when CI, TF_BUILD, JENKINS_URL or TEAMCITY_VERSION is set), so that a variable that was forgotten in a pipeline cannot change the snapshots there. To decide it in code instead, which also applies on a build server: await That(description).MatchesSnapshot().Accepting(SnapshotAcceptance.All); // missing or changed await That(description).MatchesSnapshot().Accepting(SnapshotAcceptance.New); // only missing await That(description).MatchesSnapshot().Accepting(SnapshotAcceptance.None); // never accepts Customize.aweXpect.Snapshots().Acceptance.Set(SnapshotAcceptance.New); // for this async flow Accepting(…) takes precedence over Customize.aweXpect.Snapshots().Acceptance, which takes precedence over the environment variable, so Accepting(SnapshotAcceptance.None) keeps a snapshot from being accepted while the variable is set. The setting defaults to null, which leaves it to the environment variable. To review a mismatch after a run on a build server, attach its pending file to the result of the test, when the test framework supports attachments. MSTest 4 needs the opt-in AweXpectExperimentalMSTest for it: Customize.aweXpect.Snapshots().AttachPendingFiles.Set(true); // for this async flow

By default, a text snapshot matches when it is equal apart from the newline style, and binary data when every byte is equal. A comparer decides it instead, e.g. for cover art that is rendered with slightly different pixels on every machine. Derive from SnapshotComparer in the namespace aweXpect.Snapshots: public sealed class CoverArtComparer(double minimumSimilarity) : SnapshotComparer { public override ValueTask<SnapshotComparison> CompareAsync(SnapshotComparisonContext context, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { double similarity = Images.Similarity(context.Snapshot.Bytes, context.Actual.Bytes); return new ValueTask<SnapshotComparison>(similarity >= minimumSimilarity ? SnapshotComparison.Equal : SnapshotComparison.Different($"only {similarity:P1} of the pixels are the same")); } } SnapshotComparisonContext has the Id of the snapshot (e.g. its Extension), the reviewed Snapshot and the Actual value, after the rules of the expectation were applied, e.g. with masked GUIDs. Both are a SnapshotContent like for reporters: the Bytes as the store keeps them, and the Text unless it is binary data. Use the comparer for one expectation with .Using(…), for strings, objects and binary data: await That(cover).MatchesSnapshot().WithExtension("png").Using(new CoverArtComparer(0.99)); or for all snapshots that a condition selects, with the shorthand ForExtension (ignoring the case of the extension) or with When and a predicate that sees the whole context: Customize.aweXpect.Global.Snapshots().Comparers.Set([ SnapshotComparer.When(context => context.Id.Extension == "png" && context.Actual.Bytes.Length > 1_000, new CoverArtComparer(0.99)), SnapshotComparer.ForExtension("svg", new SheetMusicComparer()), ]); The comparer of the expectation comes first, then the first comparer of the setting whose condition matches, in the order of the list, and otherwise the built-in comparison. A comparer is only called when the snapshot exists; a missing snapshot fails as before. When the comparer considers the value equal, the snapshot matches and is kept unchanged, even while accepting changes, and a leftover pending snapshot is deleted. Otherwise the failure shows its description, e.g. but it differed: only 97.2% of the pixels are the same, and the value is recorded for review or accepted like any other difference. The "Snapshot options" of the failure name the comparer, e.g. compare with CoverArtComparer (for all snapshots). Tests run in parallel, so a comparer can be called concurrently and must be thread-safe. Repeated snapshots and exceptions A snapshot that is used again in the same test run for a value with other bytes, e.g. by a repeated test, is no conflict when the comparer considers both values equal: it gets the first value of the test run as Snapshot. The first value is only kept while a comparer is set for the expectation or in the setting. An exception of a comparer or of its condition fails the expectation both ways, with the exception as its cause, and neither records nor accepts the value.

SnapshotContent.FromText(…) and SnapshotContent.FromBytes(…) create the contents like a store keeps them, so that a comparer can be tested on its own: SnapshotComparisonContext context = new(new SnapshotId("AlbumTests.cs", "Cover"), SnapshotContent.FromBytes(File.ReadAllBytes("abbey-road.png")), SnapshotContent.FromBytes(RenderCover("Abbey Road"))); CoverArtComparer comparer = new(0.99); SnapshotComparison comparison = await comparer.CompareAsync(context, CancellationToken.None); await That(comparison.IsEqual).IsTrue();

A deterministic build, e.g. with ContinuousIntegrationBuild=true on a build server, replaces the path of the repository with /_/ in the compiled code, so the path of the test file, e.g. /_/Tests/AlbumTests.cs, no longer leads to its snapshots. The package records the real path of the repository in the test assembly when it is built, so the snapshots are found in such a build as well, without any configuration.
