A snapshot is identified by the path of its test file relative to the repository, e.g. Tests/AlbumTests.cs, which is the same on every machine and in every build. This needs two things, which a usual setup provides: The test project references the aweXpect.Snapshots package, directly or through another project, as the build targets that record the path come with the package. The repository provides source control information, which the .NET SDK does for a git repository. Without them, a snapshot is identified by the full path of its test file, and in a deterministic build the expectation fails with: Failure message Expected that description matches the snapshot "/_/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.txt", but the snapshot could not be read: The path "/_/Tests/AlbumTests.cs" comes from a deterministic build, but the test assembly records no source root for it, which the build targets of aweXpect.Snapshots add. How the recorded path is found The recorded path is registered when the test assembly is loaded, by a module initializer that the source generator of aweXpect.Core adds to the test project. From a test assembly that cannot compile a module initializer, e.g. for .NET Framework with C# 7.3 or in F#, it is read when a snapshot needs it, unless the ExcludedAssemblyPrefixes exclude the assembly, e.g. Microsoft.MyApp.Tests by the prefix Microsoft. The expectation then fails with a message that names the excluded assembly, so that you can remove the prefix that matches it.

A reporter is told about the outcome of every snapshot, e.g. to open a diff tool or to collect the changed snapshots of a test run. Derive from SnapshotReporter in the namespace aweXpect.Snapshots and add it to the reporters: public sealed class ChangedSnapshotsReporter : SnapshotReporter { public ConcurrentBag<SnapshotId> Changed { get; } = new(); public override ValueTask OnMismatchAsync(SnapshotMismatch mismatch, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { Changed.Add(mismatch.Id); return default; } } Customize.aweXpect.Global.Snapshots().Reporters.Set([ .. Customize.aweXpect.Global.Snapshots().Reporters.Get(), new ChangedSnapshotsReporter(), ]); Member Called OnMismatchAsync after the store recorded a missing or different snapshot, e.g. wrote the pending file OnMatchAsync when the snapshot matches, before the store records the match, e.g. deletes a leftover pending file Like the pending file, a mismatch is only reported when the whole expectation fails, e.g. not when another branch of an .Or is met, and not for a negated snapshot. An accepted change is not reported, as it needs no review. Several reporters are called in the order of the list, and never on a build server, the same detection as for accepting changes. An exception of a reporter never changes the result of the test. SnapshotMismatch has the Id and the Store of the snapshot, the reviewed Snapshot (null when it did not exist) and the Actual value, after the rules of the expectation were applied, e.g. with masked GUIDs. Both are a SnapshotContent with the Bytes as the store keeps them (text as UTF-8 with an additional final line break), and, unless it is binary data, the Text that was compared (IsText). SnapshotMatch has the Id and the Store. The reporter is not told about files, as a store need not keep any. A store that keeps the snapshots in files, like the default store, implements IFileSnapshotStore, whose GetSnapshotFile(id) and GetPendingFile(id) return their paths: if (mismatch.Store is IFileSnapshotStore files) { Console.WriteLine($"Review {files.GetPendingFile(mismatch.Id)}"); } Exceptions of a reporter An exception of a reporter is written to the trace writer of Customize.aweXpect.EnableTracing(…) and otherwise ignored.

By default the snapshots are files next to the tests. To keep them elsewhere, e.g. in a shared folder or a database, derive from SnapshotStore in the namespace aweXpect.Snapshots: public sealed class FolderSnapshotStore(string root) : SnapshotStore { public override ValueTask<byte[]?> ReadAsync(SnapshotId id, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { string path = GetPath(id, "snapshot"); return new ValueTask<byte[]?>(File.Exists(path) ? File.ReadAllBytes(path) : null); } public override ValueTask RecordMismatchAsync(SnapshotId id, byte[] actual, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { string path = GetPath(id, "pending"); Directory.CreateDirectory(Path.GetDirectoryName(path)!); File.WriteAllBytes(path, actual); return default; } public override ValueTask AcceptAsync(SnapshotId id, byte[] actual, CancellationToken cancellationToken) { string path = GetPath(id, "snapshot"); Directory.CreateDirectory(Path.GetDirectoryName(path)!); File.WriteAllBytes(path, actual); File.Delete(GetPath(id, "pending")); return default; } public override string Describe(SnapshotId id) => GetPath(id, "snapshot"); public override string? DescribeMismatch(SnapshotId id) => GetPath(id, "pending"); private string GetPath(SnapshotId id, string kind) => Path.Combine(root, Path.GetDirectoryName(id.SourceFile) ?? "", $"{id}.{kind}.{id.Extension}"); } A snapshot is passed as bytes, which the store keeps unchanged. The library encodes the text of a string or an object as UTF-8 without a byte order mark, with an additional final line break that it removes again when reading, and passes binary data as it is, so one store keeps both. The operations describe what happened in the expectation, so the store decides how it keeps a value that awaits review apart from the reviewed snapshot: Member Called If it throws ReadAsync to read the reviewed snapshot, null if none the expectation fails with the exception RecordMismatchAsync when the snapshot is missing or different the failure names the error AcceptAsync instead, while accepting changes the failure names the error, and the mismatch is recorded instead RecordMatchAsync when the snapshot matches, e.g. to clean up the error is ignored, as the snapshot matched Describe to name the snapshot in the failure DescribeMismatch to name the recorded mismatch, null to omit ListAsync to list the snapshots of the test project for the check, null if it cannot the check fails with the exception DeleteAsync to delete an orphaned snapshot and its mismatch, while accepting changes the check names the error and continues RecordMatchAsync, Describe, DescribeMismatch, ListAsync and DeleteAsync are optional. A store that does not list its snapshots fails OrphanedSnapshots.CheckAsync(), so that a check that was asked for never passes without checking anything. A cancellation of the evaluation still aborts it. A SnapshotId consists of the path of the test file relative to the repository (SourceFile, e.g. Tests/AlbumTests.cs, see Deterministic builds), the name of the test method (MemberName), the name from .Named(…) (Name) and the environment from .UniqueFor (Variant, e.g. net8.0@windows, see Snapshots per environment). It is a record, so it can be used as a key, and its ToString() returns AlbumTests.Describes, AlbumTests.Describes.Abbey Road or AlbumTests.Describes.Abbey Road@net8.0@windows. A listed snapshot whose Variant is for another environment is skipped by the check. Extension is the file extension from .WithExtension(…) or of a FileInfo, txt by default, e.g. to choose a content type; it is not part of ToString(). Set the store for all tests, e.g. in an assembly-level setup, or only for the current async flow: Customize.aweXpect.Global.Snapshots().Store.Set(new FolderSnapshotStore("/shared/snapshots")); using (Customize.aweXpect.Snapshots().Store.Set(new FolderSnapshotStore("/shared/snapshots"))) { await That(description).MatchesSnapshot(); } The store is taken when MatchesSnapshot() is called.

Reference the package aweXpect.Snapshots.DiffEngine in the test project, and a missing or different snapshot opens a diff tool with DiffEngine, which finds the tools installed on the machine, e.g. Rider, Visual Studio, VS Code, Beyond Compare or WinMerge: .NET CLI PackageReference Central Package Management dotnet add package aweXpect.Snapshots.DiffEngine --prerelease <PackageReference Include="aweXpect.Snapshots.DiffEngine" Version="4.0.0-beta.0.pre.3" /> Directory.Packages.props <PackageVersion Include="aweXpect.Snapshots.DiffEngine" Version="4.0.0-beta.0.pre.3" /> Project file <PackageReference Include="aweXpect.Snapshots.DiffEngine" /> Latest version: 4.0.0-beta.0.pre.3 The diff tool compares the pending file with the snapshot file, e.g. AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.pending.txt with AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.txt, so taking over a change in the diff tool changes the snapshot, and the next run of the test passes. DiffEngine creates an empty snapshot file for a snapshot that does not exist yet, as most diff tools need two files. Once the snapshot matches, the diff tool is closed again. With a store of your own that keeps no files, the value and the snapshot are written to temporary files in <temp>/aweXpect.Snapshots, e.g. Tests%2FAlbumTests.Describes.received.txt and Tests%2FAlbumTests.Describes.snapshot.txt, so that the change can be reviewed; edits in the diff tool are lost there. The diff tool is never opened on a build server, the same detection as for accepting changes, nor when DiffEngine is turned off, e.g. with the environment variable DiffEngine_Disabled=true; see the DiffEngine documentation for its other options, e.g. the order of the diff tools.

The package registers a reporter by calling DiffEngineReporter.Register() from a module initializer that the source generator of aweXpect.Core adds to the test project. To register it yourself, e.g. only for some test projects, turn this off in the project file: <PropertyGroup> <AweXpectSnapshotsDiffEngine>false</AweXpectSnapshotsDiffEngine> </PropertyGroup> Then register it in an assembly-level setup of the test framework, e.g. in the constructor of an xUnit fixture or a [SetUpFixture] of NUnit: using aweXpect.Snapshots.DiffEngine; DiffEngineReporter.Register(); Register adds the reporter to the reporters that are already set, unless one is added already. Projects without module initializers A module initializer needs C# 9 and the ModuleInitializerAttribute, which .NET 5 and later provide, and which a project for .NET Framework can declare as an internal type itself. Without them, the reporter is not registered automatically; register it yourself as shown above.

Values that change from run to run, such as ids or timestamps, and values that are irrelevant for the test can be masked, converted or left out before the subject is compared, so that the snapshot stays stable. A rule starts with .For, selects what it applies to, narrows it down with filters, and ends with exactly one action: await That(album).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Guids().Mask() // numbered: {Guid_1} .For.Members().WithName("Id").Ignore(); // left out with its name The filters are combined, so a value has to match all of them. After the action, the next rule starts with .For again, or the expectation continues with .Named(…), .UniqueFor or .Accepting(…). .For.Members() and .For.Values() are only offered for a snapshot of an object, and .For.Lines() only for a snapshot of a string, so a rule that cannot apply does not compile. The text selections apply to every snapshot. The overview at the end lists all selections, filters and actions.

.For.Members() selects the members of the objects in the snapshot, at any depth. .For.Values() selects the members too, and also the items of tuples, collections and dictionaries: WithName("Id") compares the name of the member itself, exactly and case-sensitive, so it matches Id, Artist.Id and Tracks[0].Id, but not TrackId or id. The options of aweXpect's string comparison that follow apply to the name only: .IgnoringCase(), .AsPrefix(), .AsSuffix(), .AsWildcard() or .AsRegex(), e.g. .WithName("Url").AsSuffix(). For a value, the name of a tuple item is Item1, and that of a collection item or dictionary value its index or key in brackets, e.g. [0]. WithPath("Artist.Id") matches the end of the path on whole segments, compared ordinally: it matches the Id of an Artist at any depth, e.g. Albums[0].Artist.Id, but not Artist.CatalogId. The path has the format of FormattedValue.Path, e.g. Tracks[0].Id or Releases[Abbey Road]. To match the whole path from the subject, use .Which(value => value.Path == "Id"). OfType<T>() matches the declared or the runtime type, including Nullable<T> and derived types: .For.Members().OfType<DateTime>() also matches a DateTime? member and a DateTime in an object member. OfExactType<T>() only matches a value whose runtime type is T, or a null value declared as T or T?. Directly after them, OrOfType<T>() and OrOfExactType<T>() allow alternative types, see alternative types. DeclaredIn<T>() matches the values in an object of the type T or of a derived type, e.g. .For.Members().DeclaredIn<Album>().WithName(nameof(Album.Duration)) for the duration of each album, but not of its tracks. Which(predicate) and Except(predicate) decide for each value, which they get as a FormattedValue with its Kind, Name, Path, declared Type and DeclaringType; the value itself is only read when the predicate calls GetValue(). await That(album).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Members().DeclaredIn<Album>().WithName(nameof(Album.Duration)).Ignore() .For.Members().WithName("Url").AsSuffix().IgnoringCase().Ignore() .For.Members().DeclaredIn<Track>().WithName(nameof(Track.Id)).Mask() .For.Values().Which(value => value.Path.StartsWith("Artist.", StringComparison.Ordinal)).Mask("<artist>"); Ignore() leaves out a member together with its name. On .For.Values(), it also leaves out the items of tuples, collections and dictionaries, so .For.Values().OfType<DateTime>().Ignore() writes a List<DateTime> as an empty list. Select members only with .For.Members(), mask the items instead, or leave out a single item by its path, e.g. .For.Values().WithPath("Dates[0]").Ignore(). Mask() and Mask("…") replace the value, see the templates. A null value is neither masked nor converted, as it does not change from run to run. For members and values, the template can also depend on the value, which the function gets as a FormattedValue, e.g. to link ids that belong together: await That(label).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Members().OfType<int>().WithName("Id").AsSuffix() .Mask(value => "{" + (value.Name == "Id" ? value.DeclaringType.Name : value.Name.Substring(0, value.Name.Length - 2)) + "_{0}}"); Snapshot Label { Albums = [ Album { ArtistId = {Artist_1}, Id = {Album_1} } ], Artists = [ Artist { Id = {Artist_1}, Name = "The Beatles" } ] } A value for which the function returns null is kept. How the placeholder of Mask() is named The placeholder of Mask() is named after the type when the selection is filtered by OfType<T>() or OfExactType<T>() but not by WithName or WithPath, e.g. {Guid_1}, or with alternative types after the first one that the value matches, and otherwise after the member or tuple item, or Item for an item of a collection or a dictionary value.

Values of related types, such as numeric ids of int and long, are selected together with OrOfType<T>() or OrOfExactType<T>() directly after OfType<T>() or OfExactType<T>(): await That(label).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Members().OfType<int>().OrOfType<long>().WithName("Id").AsSuffix().Mask("<id>"); Snapshot Label { Albums = [ Album { ArtistId = <id>, CatalogId = "PCS 7088", Id = <id> } ], Artists = [ Artist { Id = <id>, Name = "The Beatles" } ] } A value matches when it matches any of the types, each with the meaning of its filter, so .OfExactType<Exception>().OrOfType<ArgumentException>() matches an Exception and any ArgumentException. The other filters can follow as before. Mask() names the placeholder after the first type that the value matches, e.g. {Int32_1} and {Int64_1}, so an int shares its numbers with .OfType<int>().Mask(). As the values are of different types, Convert(…) gets an object.

Members that are often empty, e.g. the bonus tracks of an album, can be left out while they are empty: await That(album).MatchesSnapshot().For.Members().WhichAreEmptyCollections().Ignore(); Snapshot Album { Title = "Let It Be", Tracks = [ "Two of Us", "Dig a Pony" ] } It leaves out each member whose value is an empty array, list, set, dictionary or other collection that knows its count, here BonusTracks = []. The filters of .For.Members() before it narrow it down, e.g. .For.Members().DeclaredIn<Album>().WhichAreEmptyCollections().Ignore(). A null value and an empty string are kept, and so are empty items of a collection or values of a dictionary, which keep their place. Sequences without a count A sequence that does not know its count, like a LINQ query or an iterator, is kept as well and only enumerated once to be written, as it might only be enumerable once.

A volatile value often has a meaningful and stable part, e.g. the year of a release date or the rounded length of a track. Convert(…) replaces the value with the result of the converter: await That(album).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Members().DeclaredIn<Album>().WithName(nameof(Album.Released)).OfType<DateTime>() .Convert(released => released.Year) .For.Values().OfType<TimeSpan>().Convert(duration => Math.Round(duration.TotalMinutes)); Snapshot Album { Released = 1969, Title = "Abbey Road", Tracks = [ Track { Duration = 4.0, Title = "Come Together" } ] } OfType<T>() types the selection, so the converter gets a T and its result type is inferred. Without it, the converter gets an object, as it does after OrOfType<T>(). The converted value is written by the formatter like any other value, e.g. a string in quotes, a number in the invariant culture and an object member-wise. The member and value rules do not apply to the values nested in it, but the text rules do. A converted null is written as <null>. A null value, or one that is no T, is not converted. Converted values under Native AOT Under Native AOT, the source generator of aweXpect.Core registers the members of the result type, so that e.g. an anonymous type is also written member-wise.

Lines that are only noise, such as durations, timestamps or banners, can be left out of a string snapshot, or replaced as a whole: await That(log).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Lines().Containing("elapsed").IgnoringCase().Ignore() .For.Lines().Containing("Track ?: *Live*").AsWildcard().Ignore() .For.Lines().Containing(@"^\d{2}:\d{2} ").AsRegex().Ignore() .For.Lines().Which(line => line.Length == 0).Ignore() .For.Lines().Containing("Now playing").Mask("Now playing: <track>") .For.Lines().Containing("Volume").Convert(line => line.Substring(0, 6)); Containing(text) selects each line that contains the text anywhere, compared ordinally like aweXpect's Contains. .IgnoringCase(), .AsWildcard() and .AsRegex() directly after it apply to this filter only, not to the comparison with the snapshot. Which(predicate) and Except(predicate) decide for each line. Ignore() leaves out the line, Mask("…") replaces the whole line with a template, and Convert(…) with the text that the converter returns for it, or leaves it out for null. The lines are handled before the text rules, so a removed line does not use up a numbered placeholder like {Guid_1}. Line breaks and regex timeouts A line ends with \r\n, \n or \r and is checked without it. A replaced line keeps its line break. A removed line takes its line break with it, and removing the last line also removes the line break before it; the other lines keep their newline style. A pattern uses the regex timeout of aweXpect; a pattern that times out fails the expectation.

.For.Text(…) selects literal text in the written snapshot, e.g. a value known at test time, and Mask("…") replaces it: await That(json).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Text(album.Id.ToString()).Mask("<album-id>") .For.Text("abbey road").IgnoringCase().Mask("<title>") .For.Text("Track ?:*").AsWildcard().Mask("<track>") .For.Text(@"(\w+\.fm):\d+").AsRegex().Mask("$1:<port>"); // "radio.fm:8000" → "radio.fm:<port>" The text is compared ordinally, unless .IgnoringCase() follows. .AsWildcard() interprets it as a wildcard pattern, where * matches zero or more characters and ? exactly one character. Unlike in aweXpect's string comparison, a wildcard does not match a line break, so that * cannot mask the rest of the snapshot. .AsRegex() interprets it as a regex pattern, and the mask can use the substitutions of Regex.Replace, e.g. $1 for the first group ($$ inserts a $). The substitutions are applied first, then {0}, so Mask("$1:{0}") counts per value of the group. Any other mask is inserted literally. An empty mask removes the text. .For.Regex(regex) takes a Regex instead, for RegexOptions, a timeout of its own or a reused static or [GeneratedRegex] instance, e.g. .For.Regex(new Regex(@"token=\w+", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5))).Mask("token=<token>"). The text rules are applied in the order in which they are written, so put a specific rule before a general one: await That(playlist).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Text(DateTime.Today.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)).Mask("<today>") .For.Text(@"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}").AsRegex().Mask("<date>"); In the other order, the general rule would already have replaced today's date with <date>. The snapshot, the pending and the accepted snapshot and the failure contain the masked value, as it is what is compared. Two values that only differ in a masked part count as the same value for the check of named snapshots. Regex timeouts A pattern uses the regex timeout of aweXpect, Customize.aweXpect.Settings().DefaultRegexTimeout (one second by default); a pattern that times out fails the expectation.

.For.Guids().Mask() and .For.Dates().Mask() replace every Guid and date with a numbered placeholder in braces, so that it stands out from the surrounding text. The same value keeps the same number: await That(log).MatchesSnapshot().For.Guids().Mask().For.Dates().Mask(); Snapshot album {Guid_1} added {Date_1} by {Guid_2} album {Guid_1} played {Date_2} A Guid is matched in the format "D" (3f2504e0-4f89-11d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301) in upper or lower case, also inside braces or parentheses, which are kept. The format "N" without hyphens is not matched, as it cannot be told apart from a hash. A date is matched in ISO 8601: a date (2026-10-17) or a date with a time (2026-10-17T09:30), with optional seconds, a fraction of up to seven digits and an offset or Z. This covers how DateTime, DateTimeOffset and DateOnly write themselves with the round-trip format "o", which the aweXpect formatter uses. Culture-specific formats, a space instead of the T and a time on its own are not matched; select them with a regex. Mask("…") replaces them with a template instead, e.g. Mask("<guid>"). The numbers are counted per subject in the order of appearance, and only after the rules that come before, so .For.Text(album.Id.ToString()).Mask("<album-id>").For.Guids().Mask() numbers only the other Guids.

The text of Mask("…") is written as it is, without quotes, unless it contains {0}: then {0} is replaced with the number of the value. Every value masked with the same template shares one counter, across all rules, and the same value keeps the same number, so relations stay visible in the snapshot: await That(album).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Members().WithName("ArtistId").Mask("{Artist_{0}}"); // ArtistId = {Artist_1} Mask() is the shorthand for the template named after the selection: Mask("{Id_{0}}") for a member named Id, Mask("{Guid_{0}}") for .For.Guids() and .For.Values().OfType<Guid>(), Mask("{Item_{0}}") for an item of a collection. That is why a Guid member masked by its type and the same Guid in a string get the same number. Braces in a template {0} is replaced as plain text, not with string.Format, so braces need no escaping: Mask("{{Artist_{0}}}") writes {{Artist_1}}, not {Artist_1}.

Paths of the environment differ between machines, so they are masked by default: // value // snapshot Loaded C:\Music\Discography\Tests\albums.json Loaded {ProjectDirectory}\albums.json Cache: C:\Users\paul\AppData\Local\Temp\abbey.tmp Cache: {TempPath}\abbey.tmp Placeholder Path {ProjectDirectory} the directory of the test project that contains the test file {SourceRoot} the source root, see deterministic builds {OutputDirectory} AppContext.BaseDirectory {TempPath} Path.GetTempPath() {UserProfile} Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.UserProfile), on every system The paths are masked before all other text rules, so these see the placeholders. Keep them for one expectation with .For.Paths().Keep(), or for all snapshots with SnapshotRule.For.Paths().Keep() in the rules for all snapshots. An expectation cannot mask them again while a rule for all snapshots keeps them; set the rules without it in a scope instead. The name of the machine and of the user are only masked when asked for, as whole words, with {MachineName} and {UserName}. The machine name ignores the case, the user name only on Windows and macOS. They are masked right after the paths, also by a rule for all snapshots, so a path in the user profile becomes {UserProfile}: await That(log).MatchesSnapshot().For.MachineName().Mask().For.UserName().Mask(); How paths are matched The longest path is masked first, as they are nested in each other, e.g. the output directory in the project directory in the source root. On Windows, a path matches with \ or / as separator, also with escaped backslashes (C:\\Music), as in JSON or in a string of a snapshot of an object; elsewhere only with /, as a backslash is part of a file name there. The rest of the path keeps its separators. Only whole segments match, so C:\Music\Album does not match inside C:\Music\Albums. The case is ignored on Windows and macOS, but not on Linux. A root of the file system, such as C:\ or /, is never masked.

Rules that apply to every snapshot are set with Customize.aweXpect.Snapshots().Rules, e.g. in an assembly-level setup. They start with SnapshotRule.For from the namespace aweXpect.Snapshots and offer the same selections, filters and actions as the rules of an expectation: Customize.aweXpect.Global.Snapshots().Rules.Set([ SnapshotRule.For.Guids().Mask(), SnapshotRule.For.Dates().Mask(), SnapshotRule.For.MachineName().Mask(), SnapshotRule.For.Regex(new Regex(@"localhost:\d+")).Mask("localhost:<port>"), SnapshotRule.For.Members().WhichAreEmptyCollections().Ignore(), SnapshotRule.For.Values().OfType<DateTime>().Convert(date => date.Year), SnapshotRule.For.Lines().Containing("Build date").IgnoringCase().Ignore(), SnapshotRule.For.Paths().Keep(), ]); They are applied after the rules of the expectation, in the order of the list, so a specific rule of the expectation goes before a general one for all snapshots. Member and value rules for all snapshots are ignored for a string subject, and line rules for any other subject. Setting a value replaces the list; to extend an outer setting, e.g. for one async flow, include it: using (Customize.aweXpect.Snapshots().Rules.Set([ .. Customize.aweXpect.Snapshots().Rules.Get(), SnapshotRule.For.Text(library.Owner).Mask("<owner>"), ])) { await That(playlist).MatchesSnapshot(); } A failure lists the rules that applied to the subject in the "Snapshot options" context, those for all snapshots marked as such, so that a rule set far away from the test is not overlooked. The context also names the comparer and the acceptance when they are set, and is left out when nothing is: Failure message Expected that album matches the snapshot "/src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.txt", but the snapshot did not exist Actual: Album { Id = <id>, Title = "Abbey Road" } Pending snapshot: /src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.pending.txt Snapshot options: - mask the members whose name is equal to "Id" with "<id>" - ignore the members whose name is equal to "PlayCount" (for all snapshots) A predicate, a mask function or a converter is described by its code, e.g. convert the values of type DateTime using date => date.Year.

The rules are applied in this order: The member and value rules, while an object is written: a rule that leaves a value out wins over every masking and converter, then the first masking or converter that matches the value replaces it, the rules of the expectation before those for all snapshots. The line rules of a string subject: a rule that leaves a line out wins, then the first matching rule replaces it. The paths of the environment, unless kept, then the machine and the user name. The other text rules in the order in which they are written, those of the expectation before those for all snapshots. Numbered placeholders share their counters across all these steps, so e.g. .For.Values().OfType<Guid>().Mask() and .For.Guids().Mask() give the same Guid the same number.

The selections and their filters: Selection Snapshots of Filters .For.Members() objects WithName, WithPath, OfType<T>, OfExactType<T>, DeclaredIn<T>, Which, Except .For.Members().OfType<T>(), .OfExactType<T>() objects OrOfType<T>, OrOfExactType<T>, and the filters of Members() .For.Members().WhichAreEmptyCollections() objects the filters of Members() before it .For.Values() objects like Members(), without WhichAreEmptyCollections .For.Lines() strings Containing(text), Which, Except .For.Text(text) strings, objects IgnoringCase(), AsWildcard(), AsRegex() .For.Regex(regex), .For.Guids(), .For.Dates() strings, objects .For.MachineName(), .For.UserName(), .For.Paths() strings, objects The actions that each selection offers: Selection Ignore() Mask() Mask("…") Convert(…) Keep() Members() ✅ {Id_1}, {Guid_1} ✅ ✅ typed by OfType<T> WhichAreEmptyCollections() ✅ Values() ✅ {Id_1}, {Guid_1}, {Item_1} ✅ ✅ typed by OfType<T> Lines() ✅ ✅ the line ✅ string → string? Text(text), Regex(regex) ✅ Guids(), Dates() {Guid_1}, {Date_1} ✅ MachineName(), UserName() {MachineName}, {UserName} ✅ Paths() ✅ A combination of the rules described above: await That(album).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Members().WithName("PlayCount").Ignore() // left out with its name .For.Members().WithName("Id").Mask() // numbered: Id = {Id_1} .For.Members().WithPath("Artist.StreamToken").Mask("{token}") // fixed text .For.Values().OfType<Guid>().Mask() // numbered: {Guid_1} .For.Members().DeclaredIn<Album>().WithName(nameof(Album.Released)).OfType<DateTime>() .Convert(released => released.Year); // Released = 1969 await That(log).MatchesSnapshot() .For.Lines().Containing("elapsed").IgnoringCase().Ignore() .For.Text(album.Id.ToString()).Mask("<album-id>") .For.Guids().Mask() .For.Dates().Mask();

Describes the possible expectations for comparing strings, objects, exceptions, binary data and files with a snapshot. Expectation Negated Summary MatchesSnapshot a string matches the snapshot stored next to the test MatchesSnapshot an object matches its snapshot, written by aweXpect MatchesSnapshot an exception matches its snapshot, written member-wise MatchesSnapshot a byte[] or Stream matches its snapshot byte by byte MatchesSnapshot a FileInfo matches its snapshot byte by byte

You can verify that a string matches the snapshot that is stored next to the test: public class AlbumTests { [Test] public async Task Describes() { string description = Describe(new Album("Abbey Road")); await That(description).MatchesSnapshot(); } } The snapshot is the file AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.txt in the directory of the test file: the first part is the name of the test file without its extension, the second part the name of the test method. Both are determined at compile time, so no reflection is needed and the expectation also works under Native AOT. The marker .awexpect-snapshot. keeps the snapshots apart from other files. Before the first run the snapshot does not exist yet, so the expectation fails with: Failure message Expected that description matches the snapshot "/src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.txt", but the snapshot did not exist Actual: Abbey Road by The Beatles Pending snapshot: /src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.pending.txt If the snapshot contained "Abbey Road by the Beatles" instead, the expectation would fail with: Failure message Expected that description matches the snapshot "/src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.txt", but it was "Abbey Road by The Beatles", which differs at index 14: ↓ (actual) "…Road by The Beatles" "…Road by the Beatles" ↑ (expected) Snapshot: Abbey Road by the Beatles Pending snapshot: /src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.pending.txt A snapshot with several lines lists every line that differs.

A string that is JSON, HTML, XML or code can be stored with a matching file extension, so that editors and diff tools highlight it: await That(json).MatchesSnapshot().WithExtension("json"); The extension replaces txt in both files, e.g. AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.json and AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.pending.json, also together with a name or an environment, e.g. AlbumTests.Describes.Abbey Road@net8.0.awexpect-snapshot.html for .Named("Abbey Road").UniqueFor.TargetFramework().WithExtension("html"). It is passed without the leading dot. Objects are always stored as .txt. A snapshot that was already used with another extension in the same test run fails, as the two files would otherwise drift apart: Failure message Expected that json matches the snapshot "/src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.json", but the snapshot was already used with the extension "txt" in this test run, so use one extension or name each one with .Named(…) or .NamedAfter(…)

Any other value is written by the aweXpect formatter, completely and indented, so that a change in a single member shows up as a changed line: await That(album).MatchesSnapshot(); AlbumTests.Loads.awexpect-snapshot.txt Album { Artist = "The Beatles", Genre = Rock, Note = <null>, Released = 1969-09-26T00:00:00.0000000, Title = "Abbey Road", Tracks = [ Track { Number = 1, Title = "Come Together" }, Track { Number = 2, Title = "Something" } ] } Members are written in alphabetical order, and nothing is shortened like in a failure message. Numbers and dates are written independently of the current culture. An object that contains itself is written as *recursive* where it repeats, and an object that is nested too deeply for the stack fails the expectation instead of being shortened. The static type decides: a string is compared as raw text, but a string in an object subject is written in quotes like any other value. A collection is written in the order it enumerates its items, except for the hash-based collections whose order can change between runs: the items of a HashSet<T>, ImmutableHashSet<T>, FrozenSet<T> or ConcurrentBag<T> are sorted by their written text, and the entries of a ConcurrentDictionary, ImmutableDictionary, FrozenDictionary or Hashtable by their key. A Dictionary<TKey, TValue> keeps its insertion order. Text rules apply to the written text, e.g. .For.Guids().Mask() for a Guid member; member and value rules, e.g. .For.Members().WithName("Id").Ignore(), apply while the object is written, see rules. Trimming and Native AOT In a trimmed application or under Native AOT, the members of the subject's type are only known when the source generator of aweXpect.Core registers them for the call site, which it does for MatchesSnapshot().

An exception is written member-wise as well, e.g. the one that a record player throws for a negative play count: public void Play(Album album, int playCount) { if (playCount < 0) { throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(playCount), playCount, "Play count must be positive.") { Data = { ["Album"] = album.Title }, }; } } await That(() => player.Play(album, -1)).Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>().Which.MatchesSnapshot(); PlayerTests.Rejects.awexpect-snapshot.txt ArgumentOutOfRangeException { ActualValue = -1, Data = { ["Album"] = "Abbey Road" }, Message = "Play count must be positive. (Parameter 'playCount')\nActual value was -1.", ParamName = "playCount" } The Message, the Data when it is not empty, the InnerException when it is set, and the other public members of the type are written, sorted like the members of any other object. An inner exception is written member-wise, too, and an AggregateException writes its InnerExceptions instead of its InnerException, which only repeats the first of them. The StackTrace, TargetSite, Source, HelpLink and HResult, and the FusionLog of the exceptions that load assemblies, are left out, as they differ between builds, runtimes, machines and Native AOT. The message of a framework exception can differ between the runtimes, operating systems and cultures: the message above names the actual value on a line of its own, with the line break of the operating system, and .NET Framework words it differently. Leave out or mask such members with the member rules, or keep a snapshot per target framework and operating system with .UniqueFor: await That(() => player.Play(album, -1)).Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>() .Which.MatchesSnapshot() .For.Members().WithName("Message").Ignore() .For.Members().WithName("ActualValue").Mask(); A failure message still writes an exception as its type and message. Custom exceptions under trimming and Native AOT In a trimmed application or under Native AOT, the own members of a custom exception, e.g. a Side property of a RecordPlayerException, are left out: the source generator of aweXpect.Core registers no type derived from Exception, because its TargetSite requires unreferenced code. The message, data and inner exceptions are still written, and so are the ParamName, ActualValue, ObjectName and FileName of the framework exceptions, which are read without reflection.

Binary data, e.g. the cover art an album service renders, is compared byte by byte. A byte[] or a Stream does not tell which kind of file it is, so it needs the extension: await That(coverArt).MatchesSnapshot().WithExtension("png"); await That(linerNotesStream).MatchesSnapshot().WithExtension("pdf"); The snapshot is AlbumTests.Cover.awexpect-snapshot.png and a mismatch is written to AlbumTests.Cover.awexpect-snapshot.pending.png, so both open in an image viewer. A Stream is read from its current position to the end; it does not need to be seekable and is neither reset nor disposed. A FileInfo is stored with the extension of the file, here pdf: await That(new FileInfo("liner-notes.pdf")).MatchesSnapshot(); .WithExtension(…) sets another one, e.g. for a file without an extension like LICENSE, which fails otherwise. A file that does not exist fails like a null subject. The failure never shows the bytes, but the first byte that differs, counted from 0, and the lengths: Failure message Expected that coverArt matches the snapshot "/src/Tests/AlbumTests.Cover.awexpect-snapshot.png", but it differed at byte 1024 (the snapshot has 4096 bytes, the subject 4100) Pending snapshot: /src/Tests/AlbumTests.Cover.awexpect-snapshot.pending.png The bytes are stored unchanged: no encoding, no additional final line break, and the newline style is not ignored. Rules do not apply to binary data: the rules for all snapshots are ignored. Names, .UniqueFor, accepting changes and the check for orphaned snapshots work as for any other snapshot. A byte[] is compared as binary data, not written by the formatter like other collections. As for a string, the static type decides, so a byte[] in an object subject is still written by the formatter. A comparer can compare it instead, e.g. tolerating small differences of single pixels. Version control must not change the line breaks in a binary snapshot, so mark its extension as binary in .gitattributes, e.g. *.png binary, unless Git already detects it as binary. A MemoryStream with C# 12 or older A type derived from Stream, e.g. a MemoryStream, needs C# 13 or later to choose the overload for streams; before, MatchesSnapshot() throws an InvalidOperationException that asks to declare the subject as a Stream, e.g. That<Stream>(stream).

The text of a string or an object is stored encoded as UTF-8. The pending file ends with an additional line break, which is removed again when the snapshot is read, so that an editor which adds a final line break does not change the snapshot. The newline style of a text snapshot is ignored when comparing, because version control can change it when the snapshot is checked out. A comparer can compare it in another way. Files that cannot be read or written, and negation A snapshot that cannot be read, e.g. because another process locks it, fails the expectation with the reason. A pending file that cannot be written is named as such in the failure, and a leftover pending file that cannot be deleted does not fail a matching snapshot. A snapshot cannot be negated: DoesNotComplyWith(it => it.MatchesSnapshot()) always fails, as accepting the pending snapshot would turn any success into a failure. Nothing is written for a negated snapshot, also not while accepting changes.

The cases of a parameterized test share the name of the test method, so give each case its own snapshot with .Named(…): [Test] [Arguments("Abbey Road")] [Arguments("Let It Be")] public async Task Describes(string title) { string description = Describe(new Album(title)); await That(description).MatchesSnapshot().Named(title); } The name is appended to the file names, e.g. AlbumTests.Describes.Abbey Road.awexpect-snapshot.txt. The same applies to several snapshots in one test method. Escaped characters and long names Characters that a file name cannot hold on every operating system (< > : " / \ | ? * and control characters), as well as % and ., are escaped as %XX in the file name, e.g. .Named("AC/DC") is stored in ArtistTests.Describes.AC%2FDC.awexpect-snapshot.txt. The same holds for @, which separates the environment (see below). A name longer than 64 characters in the file name, where each escaped character takes three, is shortened to 55 characters, followed by ~ and a hash of the whole name, e.g. Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band (Remastered Sup~e0c652ac, so that the path of the snapshot stays short enough for every file system. This applies to every name, also to one from .Named(…). A snapshot that was already used for another value in the same test run fails, so that the cases cannot overwrite each other's pending snapshot: Failure message Expected that description matches the snapshot "/src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.awexpect-snapshot.txt", but the snapshot was already used for another value in this test run, so name each one with .Named(…) or .NamedAfter(…) The same value again is allowed, so that a retried or repeated test still compares with its snapshot. Retried tests and names that only differ in case When the test framework reports retries (NUnit and TUnit), a retry may also use another value than its failed attempt. NUnit also counts the runs of [Repeat] as retries, so while accepting, a repeated test whose value changes keeps the value of its last run instead of failing. Names that only differ in case, e.g. .Named("Live") and .Named("live"), fail as well, also for the same value, as they are the same file on Windows and macOS but two files on Linux: Failure message Expected that description matches the snapshot "/src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.live.awexpect-snapshot.txt", but the snapshot "/src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.Live.awexpect-snapshot.txt", whose id only differs in case, was already used in this test run, so give them names that differ in more than the case with .Named(…) or .NamedAfter(…)

.NamedAfter(…) names the snapshot after any number of arguments of the test, which works with every test framework and under Native AOT: [Test] [Arguments("Abbey Road", 1969)] [Arguments("Let It Be", 1970)] public async Task Describes(string title, int year) { string description = Describe(new Album(title, year)); await That(description).MatchesSnapshot().NamedAfter(title, year); } The values are written in the invariant culture and separated by _, e.g. AlbumTests.Describes.Abbey Road_1969.awexpect-snapshot.txt. The name holds only the values, so that renaming a parameter keeps the snapshot, and it is escaped and shortened like any other name. How the values are written null is written as null and an empty string as "". A double or float is written with the fewest digits that round-trip, the same on .NET Framework and .NET, e.g. 0.3333333333333333 for 1.0 / 3. A date or time is written in ISO 8601, e.g. 1969-09-26T00:00:00.0000000. A collection, tuple, record or other object is written like in a snapshot, e.g. [1, 2, 3] or (4.5, "Something"), with the items of a set sorted. An object with its own ToString() is written by it, any other one with its members.

Experimental This setting is a proposal and off by default, as it changes the snapshot of every parameterized test whose cases shared one so far. With NamedAfterTestArguments, each snapshot of a parameterized test is named after the arguments of the running test case, so that its cases are kept apart without .Named(…) or .NamedAfter(…): Customize.aweXpect.Snapshots().NamedAfterTestArguments.Set(true); // for this async flow [Test] [Arguments("Abbey Road", 1969)] [Arguments("Let It Be", 1970)] public async Task Describes(string title, int year) { string description = Describe(new Album(title, year)); await That(description).MatchesSnapshot(); } The arguments are written like those of .NamedAfter(…), e.g. AlbumTests.Describes.Abbey Road_1969.awexpect-snapshot.txt. A test without parameters keeps its snapshot. .Named(…) is appended to the arguments, e.g. .Named("cover") gives Abbey Road_1969_cover, so that each case can hold several snapshots, while .NamedAfter(…) replaces them. The name has to be the same in every run, so name a test with .Named(…) or .NamedAfter(…) instead when one of its arguments is written differently each time, e.g. a Guid.NewGuid(), a DateTime.Now, a mock or any other object whose ToString() contains a random value or a hash code. Otherwise each run looks for another snapshot and fails, as it does not exist yet. Arguments of the test class, injected objects and cases written alike The arguments of a parameterized test class come first, e.g. de-DE_Abbey Road for NUnit [TestFixture("de-DE")] or TUnit [Arguments("de-DE")] on the class, so that its instances are kept apart as well. Only values are included, e.g. strings, numbers, dates or collections of them, so that an object that the test framework injects, e.g. a shared fixture, is skipped. xUnit v3 and MSTest have no arguments of the test class, and NUnit 3 does not expose them. The arguments of the test method are all written, except an injected CancellationToken, so name a test with .Named(…) or .NamedAfter(…) when the test framework injects an object into one of its parameters, e.g. with TUnit [ClassDataSource]. Two cases whose arguments are written alike, e.g. two objects whose own ToString() returns the same text, share a snapshot and fail like any snapshot that is used for another value. When the ToString() of an argument throws, the name holds the exception like a snapshot would. The running test is only known when the test framework exposes it, see the running test for the supported test frameworks. MSTest 4 marks TestContext.Current as experimental, so it is only used when the test project opts in, which also suppresses the diagnostic MSTESTEXP in the generated code: <PropertyGroup> <AweXpectExperimentalMSTest>true</AweXpectExperimentalMSTest> </PropertyGroup> Without it, the snapshot keeps the name of the test method, as without the setting.

Some output legitimately differs between environments, e.g. an exception message on .NET Framework and .NET, or a path on Windows and Linux. Keep a snapshot for each of them with .UniqueFor, and combine several by repeating it: await That(exception.Message).MatchesSnapshot() .UniqueFor.TargetFramework() .UniqueFor.OperatingSystem(); The environment is appended to the file names after an @, e.g. AlbumTests.Describes@net8.0@windows.awexpect-snapshot.txt, or AlbumTests.Describes.Abbey Road@net8.0@windows@x64.awexpect-snapshot.txt together with .Named("Abbey Road"): Option Values .UniqueFor.TargetFramework() the target framework of the test project, e.g. net8.0, net48 .UniqueFor.OperatingSystem() windows, linux, osx or freebsd .UniqueFor.Architecture() the architecture of the process, e.g. x64, arm64 The values always keep this order, whatever the order of the calls. A missing snapshot of the environment fails like any other missing snapshot; it does not fall back to the snapshot that every environment shares. A custom store receives the environment as SnapshotId.Variant, e.g. net8.0@windows. How the environment is determined The target framework is the one the build knows ($(TargetFramework)), which the build targets of aweXpect.Snapshots record in the test assembly, so .UniqueFor.TargetFramework() throws an InvalidOperationException when they are missing. On another operating system, .UniqueFor.OperatingSystem() throws a PlatformNotSupportedException.

In a C# project, the build targets of aweXpect.Snapshots nest each snapshot and pending file under its test file, so that Rider and Visual Studio show them below it in the solution explorer. How the test file is found As the names of test files and snapshots can both contain dots, the test file is the longest prefix of the file name, of up to eight parts separated by a dot, for which a .cs file exists in the same directory, e.g. AlbumTests.Describes.Abbey Road.awexpect-snapshot.txt is nested under AlbumTests.Describes.cs if it exists, and under AlbumTests.cs otherwise. A DependentUpon that you set yourself is kept, e.g. to nest the snapshots under another file: <ItemGroup> <None Update="ApiApprovalTests.*.awexpect-snapshot.txt" DependentUpon="ApiApprovalTests.cs"/> </ItemGroup> To turn the nesting off, set the property AweXpectSnapshotsNestFiles to false in the test project: <PropertyGroup> <AweXpectSnapshotsNestFiles>false</AweXpectSnapshotsNestFiles> </PropertyGroup>

A snapshot stays on disk when its test, or a case of it, is renamed or deleted. To find such snapshots, call OrphanedSnapshots.CheckAsync() once after all tests of the test project have run, in the teardown of your test framework: xUnit v3 [assembly: AssemblyFixture(typeof(SnapshotCheck))] public sealed class SnapshotCheck : IAsyncDisposable { public async ValueTask DisposeAsync() => await OrphanedSnapshots.CheckAsync(); } NUnit [SetUpFixture] public sealed class SnapshotCheck { [OneTimeTearDown] public async Task CheckSnapshots() => await OrphanedSnapshots.CheckAsync(); } MSTest [TestClass] public sealed class SnapshotCheck { [AssemblyCleanup] public static async Task CheckSnapshots() => await OrphanedSnapshots.CheckAsync(); } TUnit public sealed class SnapshotCheck { [After(TestSession)] public static async Task CheckSnapshots() => await OrphanedSnapshots.CheckAsync(); } It fails when a snapshot or a pending file of the test project is not used by any MatchesSnapshot() of the test run, e.g. after the case "Let It Be" was removed from AlbumTests.Describes: Failure message Expected that every snapshot is used by a test of this run, but 1 snapshot was not used by any test: /src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.Let It Be.awexpect-snapshot.txt While accepting all changes (SnapshotAcceptance.All, see Accepting snapshots), the orphaned snapshots and their pending files are deleted, and the check still fails, so that a deletion never goes unnoticed; SnapshotAcceptance.New only adds snapshots, so it keeps them: Failure message Expected that every snapshot is used by a test of this run, but 1 snapshot was not used by any test: /src/Tests/AlbumTests.Describes.Let It Be.awexpect-snapshot.txt (deleted) A test run that only runs some of the tests, e.g. a single test in the IDE, cannot be told apart from a complete one, so the check only runs on a build server, where the environment variable AWEXPECT_ACCEPT_SNAPSHOTS is ignored, so that it only reports. To check locally after running all tests, e.g. to delete the orphaned snapshots together with AWEXPECT_ACCEPT_SNAPSHOTS=all, force it: await OrphanedSnapshots.CheckAsync(force: true); The check cannot know about tests that did not reach MatchesSnapshot(): A skipped test, or one that fails before calling MatchesSnapshot(), leaves its snapshot unused. A test that only exists for some target frameworks, e.g. behind #if NET8_0_OR_GREATER, leaves its snapshot unused in the test runs of the other target frameworks, so only check in the run of a target framework that has all tests. A snapshot per environment (see Snapshots per environment), e.g. AlbumTests.Describes@net48@windows.awexpect-snapshot.txt, is only checked by a test run in that environment, here on Windows for net48; the test runs of the other environments skip it. Test projects that share a directory see each other's snapshots, so give each test project its own directory. Which files are checked Only the directory of the test project is searched, without bin, obj, hidden directories and the directories of other projects in it, and only for files with the marker .awexpect-snapshot., so that files of other tools are never reported or deleted. A snapshot counts as used as soon as MatchesSnapshot() is called for it, even if it is not compared, e.g. after .Or was already met. A file name that only differs in case from a used snapshot counts as used, as it is the same file on Windows and macOS.

The package aweXpect.Snapshots.PublicApi verifies the public API of an assembly against a reviewed snapshot, so that every change of the public API shows up in a pull request: await That(typeof(Album).Assembly).MatchesPublicApiSnapshot() .UniqueFor.TargetFramework(); The expectation is in the namespace aweXpect, like MatchesSnapshot(). PublicApiDeclarations.GenerateFrom(…), which generates the public API without an expectation, and the options are in the namespace aweXpect.Snapshots.PublicApi. The public API is written as C# declarations, e.g. namespace MusicStore { public abstract class Album : System.IComparable<MusicStore.Album> { protected Album(string title) { } public string Title { get; } public abstract System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable<string> Tracks(); } } It behaves like MatchesSnapshot() for strings, e.g. for the files and accepting changes.

It usually differs between the target frameworks of a library, so keep a snapshot per target framework of the test project with .UniqueFor.TargetFramework(); each target framework of the test project loads the matching build of the library. A build that the tests cannot run on, e.g. for netstandard2.0, or a reference assembly is read from its file without loading it, and named after its target framework: await That(new FileInfo(path)).MatchesPublicApiSnapshot().Named("netstandard2.0"); A build for a newer .NET than the tests run on needs the .NET SDK of that version, which installs its reference assemblies. How the types in the signatures are resolved The types in the signatures are resolved from the assemblies next to the assembly, in the output of the tests, of the .NET version it targets and of the current runtime. The NuGet packages of the library, which its build output does not contain, fill in the assemblies that are missing or only found in a lower version: they are read from the global packages folder with the versions that the deps.json next to the assembly lists. When a referenced assembly cannot be resolved, or only in a lower version, the expectation throws an InvalidOperationException that names it, instead of writing a public API that differs from machine to machine.

Options configure what is written, for the expectation and for PublicApiDeclarations.GenerateFrom(…). A failure lists the options that differ from the defaults in the "Public API options" context, e.g. ignore forwarded types.

The types that the assembly forwards to another assembly are written as [assembly: System.Runtime.CompilerServices.TypeForwardedTo(typeof(…))], as removing a forward breaks the consumers that were compiled against the assembly. They can be ignored: await That(typeof(Album).Assembly).MatchesPublicApiSnapshot(o => o.Ignoring.ForwardedTypes());

An attribute is written when consumers can see its class, or when compilers or analyzers read it by its name, e.g. [NotNullWhen(true)] or [OverloadResolutionPriority(1)], so that also a polyfill that the library declares internally is written. An attribute that is irrelevant for the public API can be ignored everywhere, by its type or, e.g. when the tests cannot reference it, by its full name like Type.FullName: await That(typeof(Album).Assembly).MatchesPublicApiSnapshot(o => o .Ignoring.Attribute<EditorBrowsableAttribute>() .Ignoring.Attribute("MusicStore.Internal.MarkerAttribute")); [Serializable], [DllImport(…)] and [Optional] are written, although the compiler stores them as flags in the metadata instead of as attributes, as removing them breaks consumers, e.g. of serialization or interop; they can be ignored like any other attribute.

A record is written with the members that the compiler synthesizes for it, e.g. Equals, GetHashCode, ToString, Deconstruct, the copy constructor and the equality operators. The members that are marked as [CompilerGenerated] can be ignored, which keeps the primary constructor, the positional properties and the hand-written members of the record: await That(typeof(Album).Assembly).MatchesPublicApiSnapshot(o => o.Ignoring.CompilerGeneratedMembers());

The public API can be restricted to namespaces, including their sub-namespaces, or to types, including their nested types, and namespaces and types can be ignored. A namespace matches whole segments, so MusicStore.Generated neither includes nor ignores MusicStore.GeneratedTools, and ignoring wins over a restriction: await That(typeof(Album).Assembly).MatchesPublicApiSnapshot(o => o .Within.Namespace("MusicStore") .Ignoring.Namespace("MusicStore.Generated") .Ignoring.Type<LegacyAdapter>()); A type is selected by its type or by its full name like Type.FullName, for a generic type with any type arguments. A nested type is written with its containing type. The filters also apply to the forwarded types. An empty namespace is the global namespace.

Every declaration is written on a single line by default. To see a change of a single parameter as a change of a single line, write the parameters of methods, constructors, operators, delegates and indexers with more than one parameter on separate lines: await That(typeof(Album).Assembly).MatchesPublicApiSnapshot(o => o.Formatting.ParametersOnSeparateLines()); So instead of public Album(string title, [System.Runtime.CompilerServices.CallerMemberName] string source = "") { } the declaration is written as public Album( string title, [System.Runtime.CompilerServices.CallerMemberName] string source = "") { }

The assembly is read with Roslyn, so the package depends on a recent version of Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp that reads all extension members correctly. A test project that needs an older Roslyn, e.g. for testing an analyzer, cannot use the package, so verify the public API in a separate test project.
aweXpect.Testably contains expectations for the file system and time system mocks from Testably.Abstractions. It is an extension for aweXpect.

.NET CLI PackageReference Central Package Management dotnet add package aweXpect.Testably <PackageReference Include="aweXpect.Testably" Version="2.1.0" /> Directory.Packages.props <PackageVersion Include="aweXpect.Testably" Version="2.1.0" /> Project file <PackageReference Include="aweXpect.Testably" /> Latest version: 2.1.0 It does not include aweXpect itself.

using aweXpect.Chronology; // from the aweXpect.Chronology package using static aweXpect.Expect; MockFileSystem fileSystem = new(); fileSystem.File.WriteAllText("let-it-be.txt", "let it be"); // verify that a file exists, together with its content await That(fileSystem).HasFile("let-it-be.txt").WithContent("LET IT BE").IgnoringCase(); // verify the properties of the found file await That(fileSystem).HasFile("let-it-be.txt").Which.HasLength(9); // verify that a file does not exist await That(fileSystem).DoesNotHaveFile("yesterday.txt"); // verify the notifications the file system raised await That(fileSystem).TriggeredNotification(c => c.Name == "let-it-be.txt"); // verify the method calls the file system recorded await That(fileSystem.Statistics).Recorded().File.WriteAllText().Once(); // verify how often the callback of a timer from a MockTimeSystem was executed MockTimeSystem timeSystem = new(); ITimerMock timer = (ITimerMock)timeSystem.Timer.New(_ => { }, null, TimeSpan.Zero, 10.Milliseconds()); await That(timer).Executed().AtLeast(3.Times()).Within(5.Seconds()); A failing expectation on the file system names the path it looked for. If the file was never written, HasFile("yesterday.txt") would fail with: Failure message Expected that fileSystem has file "yesterday.txt", but it did not exist
