As the actual value is never null, EqualTo(null) fails and NotEqualTo(null) succeeds, while a comparison of order against null, such as GreaterThan(null) or Between(null).And(3), fails even when negated.

You can verify how many lines the string has: string lyrics = """ Come together Right now Over me """; await That(lyrics).HasLineCount(3); await That(lyrics).HasLineCount().NotEqualTo(4); await That(lyrics).HasLineCount().GreaterThan(2); HasLineCount() takes the same comparisons as HasLength(). You can also verify the lines themselves. HasLines applies the expectations on the lines as a collection, so all collection expectations are available: await That(lyrics).HasLines(lines => lines.Contains("Right now")); await That(lyrics).HasLines(lines => lines.StartsWith("Come together")); await That(lyrics).HasLines(lines => lines.All().Satisfy(line => line?.Length < 20)); Lines are separated by 
, 
 or , which are all treated equivalently. A single trailing line terminator does not start a new line, so "Come together
" has one line and "" has none, matching how File.ReadLines counts the lines of a file: await That("").HasLineCount(0); await That("Come together").HasLineCount(1); await That("Come together
").HasLineCount(1); await That("Come together

").HasLineCount(2);

You can verify that the string starts or ends with a given string, or that it does not, with the same options as for equality: string title = "Abbey Road"; await That(title).StartsWith("Abbey"); await That(title).EndsWith("ROAD").IgnoringCase(); await That(title).DoesNotStartWith("Road"); await That(title).DoesNotEndWith("Abbey");

You can verify that the string contains a given substring, or that it does not, with the same options as for equality: string title = "Strawberry Fields Forever"; await That(title).Contains("Fields"); await That(title).Contains("FIELDS").IgnoringCase(); await That(title).DoesNotContain("Penny Lane"); You can also specify how often the substring should be found: string lyrics = "get back, get back, get back to where you once belonged."; // 'get' can be found 3 times await That(lyrics).Contains("get").MoreThan(1) .Because("count should be '> 1'"); await That(lyrics).Contains("get").AtLeast(2) .Because("count should be '>= 2'"); await That(lyrics).Contains("get").Exactly(3) .Because("count should be '== 3'"); await That(lyrics).Contains("get").AtMost(4) .Because("count should be '<= 4'"); await That(lyrics).Contains("get").LessThan(5) .Because("count should be '< 5'"); await That(lyrics).Contains("get").Between(1).And(6) .Because("count should be '>= 1 AND <= 6'"); await That(lyrics).Contains("help").Never(); await That(lyrics).Contains("where").Once(); await That(lyrics).Contains("back").AtLeast().Twice();

You can verify that the characters in a string are all upper or lower cased: await That("1ST PLACE").IsUpperCased() .Because("it contains no lowercase characters"); await That("1st PLACE").IsNotUpperCased() .Because("it contains at least one lowercase character"); await That("1st place").IsLowerCased() .Because("it contains no uppercase characters"); await That("1st PLACE").IsNotLowerCased() .Because("it contains at least one uppercase character"); Letters without an upper-case (lower-case) form, like ß, count as upper-cased (lower-cased). Use IncludingUncasedLetters() to also reject them and titlecase letters: await That("STRAßE").IsNotUpperCased().IncludingUncasedLetters() .Because("ß is a lowercase letter without an uppercase form");

.NET 8 or later The parsing expectations are only available on .NET 8 or later. You can verify that the string can be parsed into a type that implements IParsable<T>, and continue with expectations on the parsed value with Which: using System.Globalization; await That("42").IsParsableInto<int>(); await That("42").IsParsableInto<int>().Which.IsGreaterThan(40); await That("1,5").IsParsableInto<double>(new CultureInfo("de-DE")) .Because("the format provider is passed to `Parse`"); await That("Abbey Road").IsNotParsableInto<int>(); A failure shows the exception thrown by Parse and keeps it as inner exception. The same expectations are available for a ReadOnlySpan<char> of a type that implements ISpanParsable<T> and for a UTF-8 ReadOnlySpan<byte> of a type that implements IUtf8SpanParsable<T>: await That("42".AsSpan()).IsParsableInto<int>(); await That("42"u8).IsParsableInto<int>();

Describes the possible expectations for TimeSpan. Expectation Negated Summary IsEqualTo IsNotEqualTo equal to the expected value IsOneOf IsNotOneOf equal to one of the expected values IsGreaterThan IsNotGreaterThan greater than the expected value IsGreaterThanOrEqualTo IsNotGreaterThanOrEqualTo greater than or equal to the expected value IsLessThan IsNotLessThan less than the expected value IsLessThanOrEqualTo IsNotLessThanOrEqualTo less than or equal to the expected value IsBetween IsNotBetween between two values, both bounds included IsPositive IsNotPositive greater than zero IsNegative IsNotNegative less than zero

You can verify that the TimeSpan is equal to another one or not: TimeSpan duration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42); await That(duration).IsEqualTo(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42)); await That(duration).IsNotEqualTo(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(43));

You can verify that the TimeSpan is one of many alternatives: TimeSpan duration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42); await That(duration).IsOneOf([TimeSpan.FromSeconds(40), TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42)]); await That(duration).IsNotOneOf([TimeSpan.FromSeconds(41), TimeSpan.FromSeconds(43)]);

You can verify that the TimeSpan is greater than or less than (or equal to) another value, or that it is not: TimeSpan duration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42); await That(duration).IsGreaterThan(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(41)); await That(duration).IsGreaterThanOrEqualTo(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42)); await That(duration).IsLessThan(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(43)); await That(duration).IsLessThanOrEqualTo(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42)); await That(duration).IsNotGreaterThan(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42)); The comparisons use the signed value and not the length, so TimeSpan.FromSeconds(-1) is greater than TimeSpan.FromSeconds(-5).

You can verify that the TimeSpan is between two values: TimeSpan duration = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42); await That(duration).IsBetween(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(40)).And(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(50)); await That(duration).IsNotBetween(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(43)).And(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(50));

You can verify that the TimeSpan is positive or negative, or that it is not: await That(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(42)).IsPositive(); await That(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(-3)).IsNegative(); await That(TimeSpan.Zero).IsNotPositive().And.IsNotNegative();

The comparisons on this page, except the sign checks, accept a tolerance with Within, which widens the accepted range by the tolerance: using aweXpect.Chronology; // from the aweXpect.Chronology package TimeSpan duration = 42.Seconds(); await That(duration).IsEqualTo(43.Seconds()).Within(1.Seconds()) .Because("we accept values between 0:42 and 0:44"); await That(duration).IsOneOf([43.Seconds(), 45.Seconds()]).Within(1.Seconds()) .Because("we accept values between 0:42 and 0:44 or between 0:44 and 0:46"); await That(duration).IsGreaterThan(43.Seconds()).Within(2.Seconds()) .Because("we accept values greater than 0:41 (0:43 - 2s)"); await That(duration).IsLessThan(41.Seconds()).Within(2.Seconds()) .Because("we accept values less than 0:43 (0:41 + 2s)"); await That(duration).IsBetween(43.Seconds()).And(45.Seconds()).Within(1.Seconds()) .Because("it expands the interval by 1 second"); Without Within, the default tolerance applies, if one is configured.

Describes the possible expectations for Version. Expectation Negated Summary IsEqualTo IsNotEqualTo equal to the expected version IsOneOf IsNotOneOf equal to one of the expected versions IsGreaterThan IsNotGreaterThan greater than the expected version IsGreaterThanOrEqualTo IsNotGreaterThanOrEqualTo greater than or equal to the expected version IsLessThan IsNotLessThan less than the expected version IsLessThanOrEqualTo IsNotLessThanOrEqualTo less than or equal to the expected version IsBetween IsNotBetween between two versions, both bounds included HasMajor negated comparison has the expected major component HasMinor negated comparison has the expected minor component HasBuild negated comparison has the expected build component HasRevision negated comparison has the expected revision component

You can verify that the Version is equal to another one or not: Version release = new(1, 2); await That(release).IsEqualTo(new Version(1, 2)); await That(release).IsNotEqualTo(new Version(1, 2, 0)); An unspecified component is -1, not 0, so 1.2 is not equal to 1.2.0 and, following Version.CompareTo, less than it.

You can verify that the Version is one of many alternatives: Version release = new(1, 2); await That(release).IsOneOf(new Version(1, 2), new Version(1, 3)); await That(release).IsNotOneOf(new Version(2, 0), new Version(3, 0));

You can verify that the Version is greater than or less than (or equal to) another one, or that it is not: Version release = new(1, 5); await That(release).IsGreaterThan(new Version(1, 2)); await That(release).IsGreaterThanOrEqualTo(new Version(1, 5)); await That(release).IsLessThan(new Version(2, 0)); await That(release).IsLessThanOrEqualTo(new Version(1, 5)); await That(release).IsNotGreaterThan(new Version(2, 0)); await That(release).IsNotLessThan(new Version(1, 2));

You can verify that the Version is between two values, with both bounds included: Version release = new(1, 5); await That(release).IsBetween(new Version(1, 2)).And(new Version(2, 0)); await That(release).IsNotBetween(new Version(2, 0)).And(new Version(3, 0));

You can verify the individual components of the Version: Version release = new(1, 2, 3, 4); await That(release).HasMajor(1); await That(release).HasMinor().GreaterThan(1); await That(release).HasBuild().LessThanOrEqualTo(3); await That(release).HasRevision().NotEqualTo(5); An unspecified build or revision is -1, not 0: Version release = new(1, 2); await That(release).HasBuild(-1); await That(release).HasRevision(-1); The Has… expectations whose value is a number or a TimeSpan, e.g. HasLength(), HasCount(), HasYear() or HasMajor(), continue with one of the following comparisons, each with a negated counterpart: Comparison Negated Succeeds when the value is EqualTo(x) NotEqualTo(x) equal to x GreaterThan(x) NotGreaterThan(x) greater than x GreaterThanOrEqualTo(x) NotGreaterThanOrEqualTo(x) greater than or equal to x LessThan(x) NotLessThan(x) less than x LessThanOrEqualTo(x) NotLessThanOrEqualTo(x) less than or equal to x Between(min).And(max) NotBetween(min).And(max) between min and max, both bounds included Passing the value directly, e.g. HasMajor(1), is a shorthand for EqualTo. Comparing with null The expected value is nullable, e.g. to pass a value mapped from a property. As the actual value is never null, EqualTo(null) fails and NotEqualTo(null) succeeds, while a comparison of order against null, such as GreaterThan(null) or Between(null).And(3), fails even when negated.
